The application of Random Forest (RF) on Tetouan and Tata on datasets of 1000 and 708 samples respectively achieved good accuracy of 97% and 96.24%. The results of this study are relevant for helping planners and authorities reduce flood-related damages.

articleTitle: Simplified Modeling of Quarter and Half Car Suspension Systems Using Electrical Circuit Analogies
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, half-car and quarter-car suspension systems are modeled using an electrical circuit analogy based on the force-tension relationship, with a focus on inductive coupling, which mirrors the mechanical coupling due to the vehicle’s pitching effect. The validation is performed by comparing results from electrical circuit simulations with those from traditional mechanical modeling. MATLAB simulations generate transmissibility ratio curves for both methods, which are then compared. The study shows a strong correlation between mechanical and inductive coupling, demonstrating the effectiveness of electrical analogies for simulating vehicle dynamics.

articleTitle: Thermal Studies on Nanocellulose and Banana Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Composite
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study deals with the thermal characterization of banana fiber (BF) reinforced in an epoxy matrix, added with a fixed quantity of nanocellulose (NC) (5 wt.%) derived from rice husk by acid pyrolysis. The untreated BFs are added in 3, 6, and 9 wt.% in LY556 grade epoxy mixed with NC using an ultrasonicator and the hand-layup technique for producing the composites. The optical microscope shows the near-homogeneous distribution of BFs. The fabricated nanopolymer composites (NPCs) were characterized as per the ASTM standards. Acid pyrolysis lowers the thermal stability of NCs; BFs are good insulators that reduce the thermal conductivity of the NPCs. A reduction in conductivity by 10.25% is achieved for 9%BF addition as compared with 6%BF addition. The thermal expansion coefficient, limiting oxygen index, and melt flow index are lower for 9%BF nanocomposite by -9.80, -5.77, and -20.59%, whereas heat deflection temperature is increased by 3.81% as compared with 6%BF nanocomposite.

articleTitle: Rectangular Waveguide-Based Liquid Dielectric Characterization: A Novel Microwave Measurement Method
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a novel characterization technique for estimating the relative permittivity of a liquid dielectric material placed in a short-circuited rectangular WR90 waveguide. This technique uses the two-dimensional finite difference time domain (FDTD) method to calculate the relative permittivity based on the displacement of the first electric field node in the waveguide as measured by the MWT530 device. The results for distilled water and paraffin oil at 10.425 GHz in the X band show good agreement with those obtained using the High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) for the same materials. Compared to existing methods, this technique is simpler, faster, and more accurate for material characterization. It does not require sophisticated measurement equipment or extensive theoretical knowledge. This makes it particularly suitable for classroom teaching.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Particle Swarm Optimization and JAYA Algorithms in Estimating Electrical Parameters for Photovoltaic Cell Models: A Comprehensive Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This work presents a comparison between two widely used algorithms in the estimation of electrical parameters for photovoltaic cell models. The study focuses on evaluating the performance of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm and the JAYA algorithm. Both algorithms were assessed for extracting parameters from the double-diode model of an RTC France solar cell. Integration of an analytical procedure was implemented to constrain the search space and reduce its dimensions. The study encompasses statistical, convergence, and precision analyses. The analysis of the results generally demonstrates the superiority of PSO over JAYA.

articleTitle: Impact of Mobile Phone Usage on Delivery and Private Riders’ Safety in Marrakech
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study examines the safety behaviors of delivery and private motorcycle riders in Marrakech, Morocco, with a particular focus on mobile phone distractions. Data were collected over a two-week period at five key intersections, recording 5731 riders during peak traffic hours. Trained observers captured rider characteristics, traffic context, and unsafe behaviors at different times of day morning, noon, and evening to account for variations in traffic conditions. Decision tree analysis was used to explore the relationships between rider type, road conditions, time of day, gender, and mobile phone usage while riding. The findings revealed that private riders were more likely to use mobile phones while riding compared to delivery riders. Unsafe behaviors were influenced by environmental factors, rider demographics, and the timing of the behaviors. Significant differences in behavior were observed between private and delivery riders, with gender also playing a role in safety practices. These results highlight the need for targeted interventions, including educational campaigns to address mobile phone and policies designed for specific rider groups.

articleTitle: Robust Integral Quasi-sliding Mode Power Controller for a Variable Speed Wind Turbine under Real Climatic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Maximum wind energy extraction remains a challenge for a wind energy conversion system (WECS) because of their higher inertia moment. In this respect, this work considers the challenges of reaching an efficient maximum power extraction from the variable speed wind turbine (VSWT) by applying an integral quasi-sliding mode control (IQ-SMC) scheme. Firstly, an integral sliding manifold is proposed for the purpose of achieving maximum power extraction as well as reducing mechanical stress in wind turbine (WT). Secondly, the designed controller is tested in presence of a real wind profile. Furthermore, the proposed technique stability is analyzed by means of Lypunov function theorem and the simulation results through MATLAB platform, are also exposed and discussed, where the designed IQ-SMC controller reveal the proposed method superiority compared to the classic Q-SMC controller.

articleTitle: An Maximum Power Point Tracking Algorithm for Photovoltaic Power Systems Using the Particle Swarm Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The application of Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques is extensively studied and widely utilized in photovoltaic (PV) systems to optimize power transfer from PV panels. These optimization techniques are crucial for the efficient operation of PV systems, with various types of converters, such as boost, buck-boost and Cuk converters, playing a pivotal role. Serving as a critical interface between the PV panel and the load, MPPT circuits are essential for maximizing energy transfer. In this study, a boost converter is chosen, and a control algorithm for the MPPT controller is proposed. The MPPT implementation is based on the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) technique. To validate its effectiveness, this method is compared with a commonly used MPPT algorithm, the Perturb and Observe (P&O) method, through simulations conducted in MATLAB. The simulation results clearly demonstrate the superiority of the PSO method. It provides faster convergence, improved tracking efficiency, and reduced steady-state oscillations compared to the P&O algorithm. These results confirm the potential of the PSO method as a high-performance and reliable MPPT solution for modern photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Evaluating Reliability of equipment: The Role of Normal Distribution in Analyzing Equipment Lifetimes
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The primary challenge confronting the railway industry is the accessibility of passenger and freight vehicles. Corrective maintenance remains widespread, which means that, without proper maintenance, equipment can be used beyond its optimum service life. This leads to increased breakdowns, operational inefficiencies and unforeseen repair costs. Moreover, most maintenance practices follow a periodic approach (systematic preventive maintenance), which fails to adequately consider the actual condition of components. For these reasons, this study aims to develop a predictive maintenance strategy using a failure database from 2023, which includes an analysis of 420 railway vehicles. The study aims to show the effectiveness of the analysis of reliability data based on the normal distribution. The results underline the importance of estimating the remaining useful life of critical components, in particular the wheels, as well as the implementation of predictive maintenance to ensure safety, optimize maintenance schedule and improve availability by guaranteeing the efficiency of maintenance operations.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic-Based Load Shedding Scheme Improvement for Industrial Plants in Islanding Mode
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of an efficient load shedding technique for islanded industrial power systems to mitigate the economic and operational impacts of blackouts caused by overloading. Overloading often leads to frequency instability due to the imbalance between demand and generation, resulting in significant production stoppages and equipment damage. The technique of load shedding is used to solve this problem. In this paper, fuzzy logic control has been adapted to determine the optimum amount of load that needs to be shed based on the rate of change of frequency and the current frequency to return to the stable nominal frequency (50 Hz), thus replacing the inefficient conventional method of load shedding. MATLAB (Simulink) software was utilized to simulate the proposed method and test different load deficit scenarios.

articleTitle: Seasonal Variation of Aerosol Types and Absorption in Murcia: An AERONET-Based Study
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study leverages high-quality AERONET Sun photometer measurements collected in Murcia from December 2021 to December 2022 to investigate the seasonal variability of aerosol optical properties and identify prevailing aerosol types. The analysis focuses on two critical optical parameters: Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) and Single Scattering Albedo (SSA), exploring their seasonal dynamics across four distinct periods. The results highlight significant seasonal shifts in aerosol composition, with absorbing and scattering aerosol types exhibiting distinct temporal patterns. Desert dust aerosols were predominant in summer, driven by transboundary transport from the Sahara, whereas continental and maritime aerosols dominated during winter and autumn, influenced by local and regional sources. These findings provide a detailed characterization of aerosol behavior in the Murcia region, underscoring its seasonal variability and radiative impacts. Such insights are instrumental in refining regional climate models and enhancing air quality management strategies, particularly in the context of the Mediterranean basin's unique atmospheric conditions.

articleTitle: Self-Optimizing 6G RAN: A Unified Approach with Image and Video Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The advent of 6G wireless technology heralds a new era of network optimization driven by AI/ML algorithms across its entirety. As outlined in 3GPP TS 28.104 (Release 19), Management Data Analytics (MDA) presents diverse use cases and requirements. However, the variety of data formats and AI/ML application methods introduces complexity and limits generic implementation. Compounded by the exponential deployment of cells and a range of new devices like XR devices, UAVs, etcs., the resulting data deluge poses a formidable big-data challenge for 5G advanced, 6G, and beyond. Anticipating the unique demands of 6G, characterized by metaverse-enabled networking and AR/VR applications, there arises a need for AI/ML-driven visual data processing services. This paper presents a novel approach: representing wireless network data in the form of images and videos. Such a representation not only optimizes storage and processing requirements but also facilitates the reuse of AI/ML models across various use cases and data formats. Experimental validation is provided through two key avenues: Firstly, text-based logs are transformed into images, enabling the identification of recurrent issues through visual pattern recognition. Secondly, Comma Seperated Variables (CSV) data is converted into a series of images, effectively simulating video frames, thus extending the realm of video analytics to encompass all data types pertinent to self-optimizing networks in 6G RAN. The advantages of this image and video-based data representation paradigm are meticulously elucidated, offering a compelling proposition for the future landscape of wireless network optimization in 6G and beyond.

articleTitle: Optimizing LSTM Hyperparameters for household electrical consumption Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The effectiveness of power management is directly linked to the accuracy of the forecasting method employed. Consequently, the utilization of optimization methods can significantly enhance forecasting accuracy. This paper presents a novel hybrid method for short-term time series forecasting of household electrical consumption. By combining the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers, we aim to enhance the accuracy of electrical consumption predictions. The PSO algorithm is employed to optimize the hyperparameters of the forecasting model, which consists of stacked LSTM layers. The effectiveness of the proposed model is evaluated on electrical consumption data from a household in France with a one-minute resolution. Simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method compared to other benchmark methods, including LSTM, RNN, CNN-LSTM, RNN-LSTM, and ConvLSTM models.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of functionally graded polymer nanocomposite plates reinforced with graphene oxide powder
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper provides an analytical analysis of the mechanical buckling of functionally graded (FG) nanocomposite plates reinforced with graphene oxide powder (GOP) under uniaxial and biaxial loads. The Halpin-Tsai micromechanical model is used to derive the effective material properties of the nanocomposite plate, taking into account the continuous variation through thickness. This study comparatively evaluates four GOP distribution models uniform (U), X, V, and O to identify the most efficient approach for enhancing the structure's stability limit. The equations governing the plate were developed based on first-order shear deformation plate theory, using Hamilton's principle, and solved analytically via Navier's solution for a simply supported powder-reinforced nanocomposite plate graphene oxide (GOP). Parametric studies are performed to examine the effects of GOP weight fraction, aspect ratio, thickness ratio, and GOP distribution patterns.

articleTitle: An Edge Detection Method Based on Pixels Categorization and Complementary Transformation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new and promising edge detection approach based on pixels categorization and complementary transformation (PCCT) to improve the classical edge methods such as Prewitt, Sobel, LoG and Canny. We divide a given image on a set of regions where, some of their pixels will undergo a complementary transformation following some specific conditions. To measure the performance of the approach, we evaluate it qualitatively and quantitatively with some famous ones according to Pratt’s Figure Of Merit (PFOM) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) metrics. Experiments conducted highlight the enhanced capabilities of the newly developed method.

articleTitle: Exploring the Economic Impact of Impulse Buying in Mobile Commerce
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In developing countries, there is a lack of research regarding impulsive buying in m-commerce. Implementing a Stimulus-Organism-Response and applying Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling, the current study collected 304 samples from Gen Z and Millennial respondents in Greater Jakarta. The outcomes of this study depicted visual appeal and portability as having positive and significant relations with utilitarian and hedonic browsing (p<0.05). These findings highlight impulsive buying nuances in Indonesia’s m-commerce market. The findings also show utilitarian browsing does not affect impulsive buying (ß=0.038, p=0.549). The results can provide companies with suggestions for enhancing the visual interest of mobile interaction designs. Consumer attention can be attracted if exclusive figurines are combined with visually appealing ones. Besides that, this study highlights the importance of improving portable platforms to enhance user orientation and availability, ensuring that applications and platforms provide a smooth navigation experience across different devices. By focusing on these points, businesses in Indonesia can better understand consumers’ online purchase behavior on digital platforms. Businesses should focus on enhancing the visual appeal and portability of m-commerce platforms to attract impulsive buyers.

articleTitle: 3D Semantic Segmentation of Airborne & UAV LiDAR Point Clouds for Precise Tree Counting: a Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In a world where sustainable forest management and understanding of our ecosystems have become priorities, accurately and efficiently counting trees, especially in geographically challenging areas, has become a major challenge. This article explores an innovative approach that combines the power of machine learning and advanced technologies, such as airborne and drone lidar, to address this critical challenge. After data collection and preprocessing, we show how semantic segmentation using the "3DMASC" method makes it possible to distinguish the different classes (ground, high and medium vegetation) with remarkable accuracy. We then quantify the number of individual trees by applying, for the first time, the "Treeiso" clustering method, traditionally reserved for terrestrial data, to data acquired by airborne sensors. The comparative analysis we performed provides an unequivocal answer. Using two different datasets, one acquired by an airborne LiDAR Galaxy T1000 and the other by a Zenmuse L2 drone LiDAR, we show that the qualitative results of semantic segmentation and tree isolation are remarkably close to the ground truth. The quantitative results show significant accuracy for both datasets. In fact, for tree isolation, we achieve an error rate of less than 10% for both data types. Furthermore, the overall accuracy of the two semantic segmentation models is around 0.92.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Image Recommendation Using Siamese Neural Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In recent years, many e-commerce platforms like Amazon, Myntra, Adidas, Jumia, Temu, and others have adopted advanced recommendation systems to suggest clothing based on customer preferences. The goal is to quickly satisfy consumers while maximizing company revenues. These technologies aim to enhance the shopping experience and increase customer loyalty. Personalized recommendations help optimize sales and attract more buyers. In this work, we propose an innovative image recommendation method based on Siamese networks. The aim of this approach is to analyze the similarity between different clothing items and group similar images in the same latent space. This enhances the matching of images with common characteristics while optimizing the response time of the recommendation system. We designed a recommendation model based on Siamese networks and CNN architecture, comparing it with the most commonly used transfer learning models in the field of image recommendation. The aim of this study is to compare the performance of CNN architecture with that of transfer learning techniques. The results show better precision with a score of 0.9669 accuracy for ResNet50V2, 0.9625 for CNN, and 0.9571 for VGG19, achieved on the FashionMNIST dataset.

articleTitle: Evaluation of longitudinal crack initiation in a pressurized pipeline Using the XFEM Method
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: For decades, pipelines have played a crucial role in the transportation of gases and fluids over long distances, serving as a vital infrastructure for the efficient and reliable delivery of energy resources. However, their structural integrity can be compromised by various factors, including fatigue cracking, underscoring the importance of ensuring their safety and longevity. This study focuses on the first mode of fatigue failure, examining the initiation and propagation of a rectangular-profile crack in a pressurized tube . The influence of internal pressure variations on the distribution of stress and strain fields is investigated, along with the temporal evolution of these fields. Numerical simulations are conducted using Abaqus software in conjunction with the Extended Finite Element Method (XFEM), with the results validated against analytical calculations. The effectiveness and robustness of the XFEM approach in addressing complex crack-related problems are demonstrated through a comparative analysis with existing literature.

articleTitle: wireless Power transfer charger in islanded Mode: A Renewable Energy Integration Strategy
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper proposes a stationary wireless power transfer system for electric vehicles (EVs) powered by PV solar panels. Voltage regulation in the system is provided by a boost converter, while the inverter provides the supply to the coils, which ensure contactless energy transfer. Then, the received energy is converted to charge the battery efficiently. The Matlab/Simulink simulations show the stability and reliability of the charging process with a minimum of energy losses. This solution could show how wireless power transfer powered by renewable sources may contribute to taking off pressure from electrical grids, supporting the energy transition toward more sustainability.

articleTitle: Review of energy saving potential through waste heat recovery from thermal clothes drying processes
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Washing and drying clothes are essential components of human comfort, playing pivotal roles in public health and social interaction by maintaining personal hygiene. In many commercial laundries, tumble dryers stand out as the most energy-intensive equipment, with a significant portion of this energy dissipating into waste streams due to the absence of a heat recovery system. The aim of this paper is to conduct a literature review on enhancing energy efficiency in the thermal clothes drying process. This includes investigating the actual energy consumption of tumble dryers in commercial laundries and exploring various energy-saving approaches through efficiency analyses, including the utilization of low-cost heat exchangers.

articleTitle: Efficient Design of Rectifier Circuit for Low Power Applications at 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced approach for designing an efficient rectifying circuit for energy harvesting systems aimed at low-power applications around 2.45 GHz. The proposed rectifier based on voltage doubler topology using the SMS7630 Schottky diode is simulated under Advanced Design System (ADS) software using S-parameter and Harmonic Balance simulations. key parameters such as matching network and circuit components, are tuned and optimized to achieve a maximum RF-DC conversion efficiency and highest output voltage value. The simulation results show that this proposed circuit exhibits a wide bandwidth of 208 MHz centered around 2.45 GHz, with a high conversion efficiency of 71.015% and an output voltage of 1.31 V with an input power of 0 dBm at a load charge of 4 kilo-ohms at 2.45 GHz. Compared to previous studies, the suggested rectifying circuit demonstrates higher efficiency making it highly suitable for a variety of wireless power transmission applications such as low-power consumption devices.

articleTitle: Robust Continuous-Time MPC for Boost Converter Optimization in Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The aim of this research is to improve grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system performance by applying a comprehensive continuous-time model predictive control (CTMPC) design. To maximize power management and guarantee steady operation in a variety of environmental circumstances, a DC-DC boost converter is integrated with the predictive control approach and a highly accurate model of the PV panel. The boost converter plays a crucial role in stabilizing the system by regulating the PV panel’s output voltage and ensuring operation at the maximum power point (MPP). The simulation results, conducted under varying irradiance levels (200 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 1000 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and temperature variations (10°C to 50°C), emphasize the effectiveness of the proposed MPC-based method, demonstrating notable improvements in system stability, efficiency, and adaptability. Furthermore, potential real-world applications of the proposed approach include residential and industrial PV installations, smart grids, and electric vehicle charging stations, where precise power regulation is essential.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of 1 × 2 Circular Polarized Antenna Array Design for ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, a new single microstrip patch antenna (MPA) design is proposed using the square shape of the radiating element which is rotated by 45 degrees and incorporated by a square slot rotated by 45 degrees. The main goal behind using the slot technique in the center of the patch is to achieve the circular polarization (CP) manner and adapt the input impedance with the port. This single MPA operates at 5.8 GHz in the ISM (industrial, scientific, and medical) band. To improve the gain and directivity of this single MPA, we develop a two-element antenna array by associating two basic patches of the single MPA using the T-junction technique to a single excitation port. This array is effective in terms of a high gain of 7 dBi, high directivity of 7.10 dB, and highest radiation efficiency of about 97.34% at the resonant frequency of 5.8 GHz. In addition, this suggested antenna array operates with a good adaptation with the port of 50 Ω in terms of a reflection coefficient of -27.57 dB, and input impedance of 48.81+3.22j Ω, and it operates with a good CP manner, with an excellent axial ratio of 1.23 dB at 5.8 GHz. The proposed antenna array design is shown to be a viable solution for wireless charging systems in electric vehicles and for powering sensors and communication modules in autonomous vehicles.

Author Keywords: wireless charging systems in electric vehicles

articleTitle: Smart Cash-On-Delivery: Enhancing e-commerce transparency with smart contracts and parcel lockers
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a novel cash-on-delivery method for e-commerce, combining blockchain-based smart contracts and parcel lockers to enhance transparency, trust, and efficiency in last-mile delivery. The system reduces payment risks for suppliers while ensuring timely deliveries and tracking customers. By integrating the Internet of Things (IoT) and blockchain, this approach addresses key challenges like fraud and delivery inefficiencies, paving the way for more secure and sustainable e-commerce logistics. Furthermore, this study serves as a roadmap for other academics and blockchain professionals, encouraging further experimentation and research to refine and validate this approach through practical applications and real-world testing.

articleTitle: An Artificial Intelligence and Image Processing based approchs for evaluating Micro-scale Mechanical Properties Variations in Composite fibre bundle
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The variations in microstructural characteristics of composite fiber bundles significantly affect their mechanical performance. In this study, we propose an approach integrating image processing techniques and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate the micro-scale variations in the mechanical properties of composite fiber bundles. Microstructure image cross-sections from different positions in the fiber bundle are binarized and analyzed using image segmentation methods such as Otsu thresholding and watershed segmentation to extract key characteristics, including the local volume fraction (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>) and average fiber radius (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>). The Random Sequential Absorption (RSA) algorithm is applied, with the extracted characteristics as inputs, to model the 3D Representative Volume Element (RVE) in Abaqus. Homogenization techniques using the Finite Element Method (FEM) are employed to compute the local mechanical properties. Three machine learning models—Neural Network (NN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Regression (SVR)—are trained on the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf> values (ranging from 0.14 to 0.46) to predict the local effective mechanical properties, including longitudinal and transverse elastic moduli (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). The results demonstrate that the Random Forest Model outperforms the other models in terms of prediction accuracy, achieving R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> scores of 0.99 and 0.98 for E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> respectively. This highlights the effectiveness of the proposed method in capturing variations within fiber bundles and accurately predicting their associated mechanical properties while significantly reducing the computational cost associated with extensive FEM simulations.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling of phase change materials
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a comparison between a heat sink without phase change materials (PCM) and a heat sink with PCM, aiming to quantify the effect of the presence of PCM on the thermal management of electronic components. N-Eicosane with a melting temperature of 36.5 °C is used as the phase change material. These heat sinks generally require the use of techniques to improve heat transfer, due to the low thermal conductivity of phase change materials (PCM). An aluminum plate fin matrix is used in the present study to increase heat transfer. The performances of the heat sink matrix with and without PCM are compared. As a result, the material used in this simulation decreases the overheating effect of the heat sink (temperature pick without PCM 69 °C - temperature pick with PCM 61 °C).

articleTitle: Analysis of User Experience in the Emergency Services Portal on Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study analyzes the user experience of emergency call service portals on smartphone applications, focusing on identifying user challenges, evaluating interface design, and providing improvement recommendations. Using both qualitative like interviews, usability testing and quantitative or user surveys methods, the research found key issues such as complex navigation, unclear information, and slow response times. Many users reported frustration with complicated processes and non-intuitive designs, and difficulties accessing essential features quickly during emergencies. The study recommends simplifying navigation, improving information clarity, and optimizing response times to enhance user satisfaction and the effectiveness of emergency call services. Additionally, features such as a panic button, better visual design, and feedback options can improve usability. By addressing these UX issues, emergency call service applications can become more reliable and efficient, ultimately improving public safety outcomes. These recommendations aim to align Indonesia’s 112 emergency services with global standards, ensuring better accessibility and faster assistance for users in critical situations.

articleTitle: Modernizing Agricultural Training in Chad: An Integrated Architecture Based on VXLAN, SDN and Zeroconf for Inclusive Rural Development
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The research presents an innovative technological solution to modernize agricultural training in Chad, integrating VXLAN, SDN, and Zeroconf to overcome infrastructure challenges and digital illiteracy in rural areas. By creating a secure, flexible, and accessible virtual network, this approach addresses the specific needs of the Chadian agricultural sector, where 80 % of the agricultural population is illiterate. The proposed architecture provides robust connectivity, centralized resource management, and simplified technological access, opening new perspectives for rural development and digital inclusion. Future prospects include extending this solution to other African regions, developing tailored training modules, and evaluating its socioeconomic impact, positioning this research as a significant contribution to modernizing agriculture in resource-limited contexts.

articleTitle: A comparative study of different control strategies for trajectory tracking of a quadrotor UAV
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to study, analyses and design multiple control strategies for trajectory tracking of an underactuated quadrotor. Using the Newton-Euler method, a basic nonlinear dynamic model has been derived for a quadrotor with six degrees of freedom, and then used to test the designed control system. The work discusses different stabilization methods, such as PD control, Sliding Mode Control, and the Super-Twisting SMC. The performance of the control methods was evaluated using simulations, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of the super twisting control strategy proposed for the quadrotor.

articleTitle: Numerical Buckling Analysis of Hemp Fiber-Reinforced Hybrid Composites in Wind Turbine Blades
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The static analysis of the structure is not sufficient to test its stability under static loads, and a buckling analysis is necessary. In this paper, an optimal wind turbine blade made of epoxy resin reinforced with hemp/glass fiber was designed using the BEM method, analyzed using the finite element method with Patran®/Nastran® software, and a buckling analysis was performed under the ultimate load case corresponding to a Class I wind velocity (70 m/s). The results show that the buckling load factor for the 1st mode is greater than 1, indicating that the structure is safe, and that buckling does not occur.

articleTitle: Development of Ultrasonic Radar System for Object Detection Using PIC 16F877A
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Ultrasonic radar represents a promising technology, offering reduced cost while combining efficiency and versatility. This project details the design and implementation of a radar system based on the PIC 16F877A microcontroller, capable of measuring both the distance and direction of objects in their environment. To achieve this, an ultrasonic sensor is used in combination with a stepper motor, enabling the system to scan a full 360° area. The collected data is then displayed in real-time on an LCD screen, providing clear and precise visualization of the information. The system also integrates LEDs that serve as visual indicators to signal the proximity of detected objects. When objects are at critical distances, a buzzer is activated to alert the user, adding an auditory dimension to the detection. This feature is particularly useful for applications requiring rapid response, such as surveillance, automotive, or navigation. Comprehensive tests were conducted to evaluate the system's performance. These tests included both stationary and moving targets, allowing for the verification of reliability and measurement accuracy under various conditions. The results showed that the distances measured by the system had minimal deviations from the actual distances, confirming the high precision of the device.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Machine Learning Models Applied to PdM
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Thanks to the development of Industry toward digitalization, predictive maintenance (PdM) guidelines are now applied to manage availability, downtime, component utilization rates, equipment lifespan and their maintenance costs, using technologies such as Internet of Things (IoT) devices and artificial intelligence. Data collection through communication networks enables the acquisition of massive amounts of data on equipment conditions and operational processes allowing for automated fault diagnostics after detecting anomalies by analyzing information from pre-installed sensors in the equipment. This paper presents a comparative analysis of machine learning (ML) models extensively applied to PdM. It compares machine learning models based on the most commonly used criteria in PdM and industrial equipment while highlighting the main contributions of researchers, thus offering directions and opportunities for future research.

articleTitle: Combining Temporal and Spectral Features for Improving Hand Gesture Classification from sEMG Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Robotic prosthetic hands are being developed to restore some individuals’ capacity to manipulate objects in their daily lives. Currently, more focus is being placed on applying machine learning algorithms to enhance the dexterity of myoelectric prostheses; due to their high precision and sophisticated control capabilities. These algorithms aim to identify and classify hand gestures from a surface electromyography (sEMG), which will be used later as a command of an object. In this work, we suggest a method for categorizing different hand gestures. One of the advantages of this approach is that it can perform well based on a few features from both the time and frequency domains. We use these features with two well-known machine learning algorithms in the literature: Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). Subsequently, we assess how well these algorithms perform using a multi-channel sEMG dataset comprising hand gestures simulated by 40 participants, including movements such as the neutral state, wrist extension and flexion, grip, ulnar and radial deviation, abduction and adduction of all fingers, supination, and pronation. Four sEMG signal channels are used to record these gestures. SVM attained an accuracy of 95.94%, whereas KNN achieved 95.5%, according to the average accuracy rates derived from 40 subjects and 10 hand movements.

articleTitle: Testing Environment for Validating Swarm Algorithms in Randomized Settings
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Inspired by the collective behavior of organisms such as bee swarms and bird flocks, swarm algorithms are employed in artificial intelligence to tackle complex problems through the collaboration of multiple agents. This paper presents a digital validation environment designed to assess the performance of swarm algorithms. Two prominent algorithms were examined: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Directional Pheromone Walk (DPW). Given its effectiveness in territory exploration, DPW was selected for this study. Implementation was carried out using the open-source Crazyflie drone. The digital validation environment allows for the simulation and exploration of randomized terrains, facilitating the appropriate selection of swarm algorithms. The proposed integration with hardware enabled rapid and efficient system implementation, demonstrating a robust approach to algorithm validation in virtual environments. This setup allows users to optimize battery usage, costs, and the number of drones in advance for practical system deployment.

articleTitle: A Design of a Compact Coplanar Low Pass Filter for THz applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a new configuration of a coplanar compact low pass filter (LPF) for terahertz applications based on coplanar-waveguide (CPW). It features a compact size with dimensions of 84.38 by 125.60µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The filter is mounted on a GaAs substrate having a thickness of 30 µm, a dielectric constant of 12.9 and loss tangent of 0.0001. The filter's cut-off frequency is 0.45 THz, and it exhibits a rejection outside the bandwidth below 20 dB. The design's validity is confirmed through simulations using two independent electromagnetic solvers, highlighting its potential for applications in terahertz imaging, non-destructive testing, satellite communications, medical diagnostics, and biosensing.

articleTitle: Evolution of the bistatic acoustic response obtained at oblique configuration from a bilaminated cylindrical shell
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The analysis of the acoustic signal scattered at normal incidence by an elastic mono-layered cylindrical shell in a bistatic configuration (i.e., the transmitter and receiver are positioned at different locations), indicates the potential of this method to detect and locate defects in comparison with the monostatic method (i.e., the transmitter and receiver are positioned at the same locations). In addition, the bistatic method at normal and oblique incidence enables the identification of the mode of vibration n (n represents the required number of wavelengths around the circumference of the shell to excite a given resonant frequency) of the guided surface waves that propagate around and along the cylindrical shell. The primary objective of this study is to investigate the impact of receiver position (azimuthal angle θ) on acoustic scattering from an obliquely excited aluminium/stainless steel (Al/SST) bilaminated cylindrical shell immersed in water and filled with air. Frequency analysis of the signals collected at different positions of the receiver revealed that the frequency content of these signals is dependent on the θ angle. In addition, we investigate the evolution of these signals using other representations such as the temporal representation, modal identification plan, angular diagram, and azimuthal angle-frequency representation. Owing to the symmetry of the problem, most of the numerical results presented in this paper are primarily derived from half-turns (0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°) in increments of 1°. Furthermore, the findings obtained through the bistatic approach were compared with those derived from the special case of θ = 180°, where the angle of incidence was maintained at α = 12°.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the influence of backsheet thickness on the performance of silicon photovoltaic modules
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The thermal management of photovoltaic (PV) modules is highly dependent on the physical properties of their constituent layers, particularly the back sheet (Tedlar). This study proposes a three-dimensional numerical analysis, developed in COMSOL Multiphysics, to assess the impact of Tedlar layer thickness on the thermal and electrical performance of a silicon PV module. Three thicknesses (0.3 mm, 1.6 mm, and 3.2 mm) were studied under different climatic conditions, with irradiance ranging from 300 to 1100 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and ambient temperature from 20 to 36°C. The results showed that the module’s solar cells had the highest temperature and that the temperature of the rear surface was higher than that of the front. Increasing the thickness of the rear sheet leads to a more marked rise in cell temperature, from 49.02°C to 51.3°C when the thickness varies from 0.3 mm to 3.2 mm, for an irradiance of 1100 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Ambient temperature also has a direct effect, increasing cell temperature from 45.28°C to 60.23°C when the temperature rises from 20°C to 36°C. In terms of power, this drops from 210.59 W to 197.27 W when irradiance varies from 300 to 1100 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> but decreases slightly with increasing Tedlar thickness. Electrical efficiency drops by 0.15% with increasing Tedlar thickness, for an irradiance of 1100 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and an ambient temperature of 24°C. These results confirm that the thickness of the Tedlar layer is an important lever for improving module performance, particularly under severe climatic conditions.

articleTitle: Implementation of Deep Learning models on an FPGA board for voice classification
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of an intelligent door security system, based on voice classification of people requesting access to datacenter rooms, by applying deep learning models (CNN and RNN) implemented on an FPGA board. Our approach is to use the ZYBO Xilinx-Zynq7000 FPGA board, which integrates the PYNQ framework and enables the use of the PetaLinux operating system, to facilitate the deployment of our deep learning models on the FPGA board. We also use deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow and Keras for model development and training. We add the MFCC (Mel Frequency Cepstrum Coefficient) layer to extract parameters features to describe the voice in form of data. The results of this work demonstrate that the ZYNQ FPGA board is well suited to parallel computation of deep learning models (CNN and RNN) for real-time applications, with the highest accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Consumption Predictions Using ANFIS method
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study investigates the application of the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) for predicting energy consumption, leveraging its unique combination of neural networks and fuzzy inference systems. The research focuses on the integration of historical energy consumption data with influencing factors such as time-related variables, weather conditions, and occupancy levels. By harnessing the adaptive learning capabilities of neural networks alongside the reasoning power of fuzzy logic, ANFIS effectively models complex, nonlinear relationships inherent in energy usage patterns. The performance of ANFIS is compared to traditional forecasting methods, highlighting its enhanced accuracy and robustness in handling uncertainty and imprecision in real-world data. The findings suggest that ANFIS can significantly improve energy management strategies, offering valuable insights for optimizing resource allocation and reducing consumption.

articleTitle: The impact of augmented reality on the understanding of assembly drawings: case study of a gear train
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: augmented reality (AR) has shown enormous potential as a teaching tool for improving comprehension in technical and engineering fields. This research investigates the influence of AR on the comprehension and interpretation of assembly drawings, with a concentration on gear train assembly drawing. We created an AR-based web application called GTAR (Gear Train with Augmented Reality), using CATIA CAD software, AR-JS is an innovative platform intended for the development of AR experiences on the Web and GitHub is a development platform permitting developers to write, save, control, and share their code. The AR-based web application enables students to see animated simulation of gear train system on their smartphones. This tool aims to link static representations with functional comprehension through the integration of dynamic visuals into conventional technical drawings. This article discusses the making process of the AR-based web application, its educational advantages, and the outcomes of an experimental research study conducted with the second year of the mechanical science and technology baccalaureate students at a technical high school in Casablanca, Morocco. Initial results indicate that AR enhances spatial thinking, reduces cognitive strain, and elevates precision in reading assembly details. Post-test findings indicate a significant improvement in the average score, approximately between 15 and 16 points. This extensive enhancement demonstrates the beneficial impact of AR on students' comprehension of the assembly drawings.

articleTitle: Distributed Caching System in a Decentralized Network of Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is evolving rapidly, with countless connected devices generating and exchanging data in real-time. However, managing this data efficiently while considering network constraints, energy consumption, and storage limitations remains a challenge. In this work, we introduce a distributed caching mechanism that allows IoT objects to build co-location relationships and optimize data storage. By clustering objects based on their locations and characteristics, we enable smarter data caching and retrieval, reducing delays and improving network performance. Our approach selects caching nodes based on key factors such as centrality, popularity, energy, and storage capacity, ensuring efficient data handling. The results show that our method significantly improves network lifetime, reduces latency, and enhances overall system efficiency compared to traditional approaches.

articleTitle: The Impact of Quality Standards on Educational Processes and their Digitalization A Step Towards Better Training
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: A quality standard is a normative framework that defines the essential criteria for assessing the quality of education. It aims to improve the performance of higher education institutions. The reference systems influence teaching methods, the organization of teaching and teacher training. They promote a student-centered approach and employability. The establishment of a repository requires in-depth reflection on the objectives of education. Assessment tools are developed to measure compliance with the repository. However, its adoption raises debates on standardization versus local adaptation. Repositories contribute to the internationalization of education. However, they can be criticized for their rigidity. Implementing a repository requires a supportive organizational culture. Its impact on the quality perceived by students remains to be explored. In conclusion, quality frameworks provide a framework for improving education, but their effectiveness depends on how well they are implemented.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance of Straw–EPSB Composites for Sustainable Building Insulation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The building sector significantly contributes to global energy consumption, largely due to heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems. This study explores the development of eco-friendly straw-based composite insulation materials using waste expanded polystyrene (EPS) as a binder. In this approach, EPS waste is dissolved in a cellulose-based solvent to create a glue-like substance that is subsequently mixed with straw. The thermal properties of the resulting composites were evaluated using a transient hot-disk technique. Results indicate that increasing the straw fraction in the composite reduces both density and thermal conductivity, thereby enhancing its thermal insulation performance. In particular, the optimal formulation, designated as MSTE70 (30% binder, 70% straw), achieved a thermal conductivity of 0.0817 W/m.K, and density of 226.5 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and a specific heat capacity of 2028.72 J/kg.K. Furthermore, a dynamic TRNSYS simulation conducted on a small office building in Oujda, Morocco, indicated that integrating MSTE70 insulation reduced annual energy consumption by approximately 56%. These findings suggest that straw–EPS (MSTE) composites offer a promising sustainable alternative to conventional insulation materials, effectively balancing thermal efficiency and environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Transcriptional analysis of human cell organoids for the identification of gene signatures associated with Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a disorder that affects the neurological system during the developmental stage due to environmental, neurobiological, or genetic factors, leading to deficits in social communication, repetitive and stereotyped behaviors. Several groups of ASD are identified based on head circumference (macrocephaly and normocephaly) or on the onset of symptoms (early onset and regression). The aims of this study were to compare the genetic expression of cell organoids from one individual with ASD and two healthy controls, and identify genes involved in this disorder. to achieve these goals, Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets generated from organoids developed from induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines constructed with peripheral blood of two normal controls and one individual with ASD selected from the Jiangsu Birth Cohort Study (JBC) were analyzed using Seurat package version 5.2.1. The results show that several genes are overexpressed (NEUROD6, NNAT, PCDHB5, B3GAT2…), and others are down expressed (LDOC1, CHCHD2, BST2, PMEL…) in ASD cells compared to normal controls. These genes could be of great interest to develop potential biomarkers for the early diagnosis of ASD, for defining an action plan to address this disorder.

articleTitle: Design of a Secondary On Board Charger Based On Push Pull DC DC Converter Fed By a Standalone PV Station
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a secondary high-power charger provided by a photovoltaic source with grid connection. The high-power charger is composed of Push-Pull DC-DC converter controlled by a constant voltage constant current algorithm based on PI control. The first stage is composed of a PV panel source, controlled by a fuzzy logic using a MPPT algorithm, associated with a synchronous boost converter to set up the voltage at the standard common 400V bus level. While the charger is a second stage composed by a push-pull dc-dc converter for step down and adapting the voltage and the charging current for the battery of the urban electric car. Thus, to achieve this goal, a simulation results of the proposed configuration control techniques by using MATLAB/Simulink environment, are presented and discussed at the end of this paper.

articleTitle: Multi-objective workflow scheduling optimization for energy efficiency in cloud computing
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Task scheduling in cloud computing systems is a critical and challenging problem requiring decisions regarding resource allocation to tasks to optimize a performance criterion. This problem has required researchers and developers to overcome significant challenges. Our goal in this paper is to minimize the makespan and reduce energy consumption in cloud computing systems by efficiently scheduling workflows.To achieve this, we first proposed a dynamic multi-objective modeling which is transformed into a mono-objective one using dynamic weights. Then, we proposed a dynamic genetic algorithm (DGA) to solve the problem.The results are compared with the HEFT algorithm and signifi-cantly reduced the total energy consumption.

articleTitle: Assessing the performance of artificial intelligence regression models for predicting the fatigue of a bio-based composite
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The demand for natural fiber-reinforced composites in engineering design has increased, offering advantages like low density and environmental benefits. However, their long-term behavior, particularly under cyclic loading, remains limited. This study aims to predict the fatigue behavior of composites reinforced with natural fiber using several predictive models of regression trained on a database of studies. This model reduces experimental testing and improves prediction quality by avoiding computationally intensive data points.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Based Optimal FTSMC for Longitudinal Control of an Autonomous Vehicle Using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Effective control of vehicle longitudinal dynamics is essential for enhancing stability and performance. This study introduces a Fixed-Time Based Optimal Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control (OFTSMC) designed to provide robust and fast convergence. The controller parameters are optimized through the application of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The fixed-time convergence is ensured by applying the Lyapunov approach to analyze system stability. The initial step consists of developing the mathematical model representing the vehicle’s longitudinal dynamics. The proposed method is then implemented and validated through both simulations in MATLAB/Simulink and real-world testing on a Four-Wheel Drive (4WD) vehicle using an Arduino Uno. The experimental and simulation results confirm the controller’s ability to provide precise and accurate performance, demonstrating its suitability for practical applications in vehicle dynamics control.

articleTitle: Effects of quantum confinement and hydrostatic pressure on electronic properties of diluted magnetic double quantum well
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The goal of this work is to analyze the electronic characteristics of diluted magnetic (DM) system containing a localized magnetic impurity (MI), under the impact of quantum confinement and hydrostatic pressure (HP). We worked out the Schrödinger equation using the variational method and the effective mass approximation (EMA). Our results reveal a strong dependence of the electronic characteristics on the aforementioned effects. The findings provide a deeper understanding of how DM low-dimensional systems could have significant implications for future device applications.

articleTitle: Synchronization Control of Heart Rhythm Dynamics with Interval Time-Varying Delays*
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The dynamics of cardiovascular rhythms are of great interest because of the central role of the heart in the physiology of living organisms. These rhythms can be either periodic, reflecting normal functioning, or chaotic, associated with pathological conditions. This paper addresses the problem of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> synchronisation control applied to a chaotic heart rate system with time-varying delays at the input. A Takagi-Sugeno type fuzzy approach is used to model this system. New conditions in the form of linear matrix inequalities are established to ensure robust stability analysis and to design an output feedback gain based on a less conservative condition for stability evaluation of Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy systems. The results obtained indicate that the proposed control scheme effectively synchronizes the pathological heart rhythm dynamics of a patient with a reference heart rhythm dynamics.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Resonant WPT Systems for Wireless Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The wireless technology for EV charging is a promising technology that offers greater convenience and flexibility compared to traditional plug-in charging systems. This paper conducts a circuit analysis for both resonant and inductive WPT systems, compares their efficiency, outlines the specific characteristics of the resonant WPT system, notably investigating the impact of coupling and quality factor, and bifurcation phenomenon on the system, and finally concludes with a conclusion.

articleTitle: Real-Time Detection and Correction of Signal-Based Attacks in Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) are vital to modern infrastructure but remain vulnerable to signal-based attacks that threaten their reliability and safety. This work proposes a practical security framework combining Verilog simulations and Python-based analysis to detect and correct False Data Injection (FDI) attacks in real time. The system integrates anomaly detection, classification, and, correction using predefined logic and Machine Learning (ML) inference. Experimental results demonstrate a 92.3% detection rate, 5.4% false positive rate, and correction latency under 250 ms. Three simulated attack scenarios confirm the framework’s robustness and ability to sustain CPS performance under adversarial conditions. Future work will explore Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) deployment for hardware validation and Digital Twin (DT) integration for realtime system mirroring and predictive defense.

articleTitle: A comparison of grid-connected photovoltaic systems using P&O and Fuzzy Logic MPPT algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Photovoltaic solar energy, derived from solar radiation, has become one of the most widely used renewable energy sources in recent years. In this paper, we compare two MPPT control algorithms, P&O and fuzzy logic, in a grid-connected photovoltaic solar system. A DC/DC Boost converter is used to optimize power by providing a higher continuous voltage, while an inverter converts this energy into alternating current, which is injected into the grid. The goal is to generate clean energy to supply electrical loads or inject any surplus into the grid.

articleTitle: Quantifying Uncertainty in Energy Demand Forecasts: A Probabilistic Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to energy demand forecasting through the implementation of a probabilistic deep learning framework that explicitly quantifies prediction uncertainties. We develop a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural network architecture enhanced with Monte Carlo dropout for probabilistic predictions. The model demonstrates robust performance in forecasting hourly energy consumption patterns while providing reliable uncertainty estimates. Our results show significant improvements in prediction accuracy, achieving an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.8547 and a mean absolute error of 0.0412, while successfully capturing both aleatory and epistemic uncertainties in the predictions. The proposed framework offers valuable insights for grid operators and energy policymakers, contributing to more reliable and efficient energy management systems.

articleTitle: Harmonic/Interharmonic Detection and Estimation based-SimPowerSystems for Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents new methodologies for the detection and estimation of harmonics and interharmonics in data sets, using specialized technology libraries from Simscape Power Systems (SPS). A dedicated MATLAB script has been developed to analyze each phase by simulating short-circuit faults on a standard IEEE reference base. Various direct, inverse and homopolar harmonic components are generated and randomly injected at different points of the test network. During simulation, current and voltage signals from the buses are recorded at a frequency of 20 kHz, creating a rich database for automatic learning. This method, which can be extended to more complex networks and higher harmonic orders, extracts precise characteristics in terms of frequency, amplitude and onset/disappearance time. It is also adaptable to non-standard networks modeled in Simscape. The proposed approach thus modernizes and enhances advanced harmonic phase detection (HPD) and estimation (HPE) techniques, while implementing an efficient time-delay (TD) method for fault detection. Finally, the resulting database provides a reliable basis for training robust models and implementing critical protection functions.

articleTitle: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Configuration Method for Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly being used for many different domains from food delivery services and fireworks shows to war and military scenarios. UAVs can be used for different purposes and in different conditions. Therefore, it becomes important to standardize how UAV flights can be configured when they encounter different types of flight zones in 5G networks. In this paper, we propose a novel function: the UAV Location Restriction Mapper Function (ULRMF) that provides a method for communicating UAV flight configurations to the UAV and to assess UAV flight security violations and deviations.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Efficiency Circularly Polarized Antenna Array for Microwave Power Transmission Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced single antenna (SA) design utilizing microstrip technology. The SA’s patch is designed in a square shape which is capable of operating with circular polarization (CP) at 2.45 GHz. To enhance the CP performance, two techniques are incorporated: the slot technique and the slit technique, which also improve the overall performance of the SA. Building upon this SA design, a three-element antenna array is developed, followed by the design and analysis of a six-element antenna array using three software tools (CST MWS, HFSS, and ADS) to validate its effectiveness. The primary objective of the six-element array is to achieve superior gain, directivity, and radiation efficiency compared to both the SA and the three-element array designs. This six-element antenna array is well-matched with the port excitation in terms of the reflection coefficient of -32.65 dB, and the input impedance of 47.15 Ω at 2.45 GHz. In addition, this array has good performance in terms of high gain of 9.09 dBi, high directivity of 9.19 dB, and high radiation efficiency of 97.16% at 2.45 GHz. Also, this array operates in a CP manner with an axial ratio of 1.61 dB. A comparative study is given to demonstrate the benefits of the proposed antenna array with those of existing designs. The proposed antenna array is considered an efficient and eco-friendly solution for feeding small electronic devices across multiple applications.

articleTitle: Alignment of COBIT 5 and ITIL v4 Frameworks Through an Ontology: Towards Improved Maturity of IT Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In Moroccan universities, information technology (IT) plays a key role in establishing effective IT governance. However, the evaluation of COBIT 5 DSS (Delivery, Service, and Support) processes reveals a low maturity level (level 2), reflecting inefficient use of IT services. The adoption of ITIL v4 emerges as an essential solution to address these challenges but requires a clear definition of the relationships between COBIT processes and ITIL activities. This research proposes an integrated ontology aligning COBIT and ITIL v4, aiming to improve process maturity and create IT value. This model promotes resource optimization, proactive governance, and digital transformation tailored to the specific needs of Moroccan universities. By leveraging real-time evaluation mechanisms, it provides a structured and transferable approach to enhance the effectiveness of information systems and support academic competitiveness.

articleTitle: Development of an ultra-wideband patch antenna in the form of a decagon for mobile applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper is based on the design of a 40×30×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> decagonal multiband patch antenna with a copper body and a 1.6 mm thick FR4 substrate for consistent electrical properties and thermal stability. It is designed using HFSS software for UWB mobile applications, with a frequency band between 2.02 GHz and 11.12 GHz. The innovative design allows the antenna to be compact while covering a wide range of frequencies for all WLAN applications. The antenna can operate with multiple telecommunications standards, namely, LTE, RFID, Bluetooth, WLAN, Wi-MAX, C-band, and a portion of the X-band.

articleTitle: AI-Optimized Genetic Algorithm for Enhancing Resource Recovery in the Circular Economy
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a Genetic Algorithm (GA)- based optimization approach aimed at improving circular economy strategies by optimizing recyclability and economic value, while minimizing disassembly complexity and environmental impact. A multi-objective function is established, incorporating essential parameters such recyclability rate, component reuse value, disassembly expenses, carbon footprint, and waste minimization. The GA investigates an optimal balance between sustainability and economic viability using an evolutionary search method that identifies and enhances solutions throughout several generations. The dataset comprises 50 components of end-of-life products, categorized as metals (40%), plastics (30%), and electronic materials (30%), exhibiting recyclability rates between 35% and 95%. The results indicate that the GA attains a 25% enhancement in recyclability, a 30% reduction in disassembly complexity, and a 20% decrease in carbon footprint relative to traditional approaches. The suggested method offers a versatile and scalable decision-making instrument for manufacturers, recyclers, and policymakers, enhancing a more sustainable resource recovery system.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Evaluation and Prediction of the Stability of Civil Engineering Structures: Case Study of the Iminifri Natural Bridge, Demnate, Morocco
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study applies artificial neural networks (ANNs) to predict the deformation of the Iminifri natural bridge in Demnate, Morocco. Using real-world data for compressive strength (RC), cohesion, and Young's modulus as inputs, and deformation (in meters) as the output, we employed a Monte Carlo simulation with 1000 iterations (70% training, 15% validation, 15% testing). The resulting ANN model achieved a mean squared error of 0.0239 and a regression coefficient of 0.999, indicating high accuracy. The study concludes with a discussion of the findings, limitations, and potential future research directions.

articleTitle: A comparative study of four methodologies for parameter estimation in photovoltaic cells
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: To assess the energy efficiency of a photovoltaic device, a precise extraction of the electrical parameters from its equivalent circuit is essential to comprehensively describe the curve representing its current-voltage characteristic. In this context, the present study provides a comparative analysis of four widely employed methods in the literature for identifying the single diode model. Of these four methods, two are analytical, while the other two involve iterative approaches. The assessment of each method's performance relies on comparing its results with experimental data. Criteria such as mean square error and absolute error are also introduced to evaluate the inherent precision of each method.

articleTitle: CFD Simulation of Brine and Wastewater Mixing : Optimizing Environmental Impact in desalination Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study presents a detailed simulation-based investigation of the mixing process between high-salinity brine from desalination plants and effluent from wastewater treatment facilities. The objective is to explore optimal conditions that promote the diffusion of brine into the wastewater stream, thereby reducing the overall salinity and mitigating the environmental impact of brine discharge.
