A two-dimensional CFD simulation was carried out to evaluate the effect of different configurations on the dilution efficiency. The results demonstrated a significant improvement in salinity reduction, effectively bringing the outlet concentration below the environmental threshold considered safe for marine ecosystems. Brine discharges from desalination plants can reach salinity levels as high as 60 000 PPM, which poses a serious threat to marine ecosystems and disrupts environmental balance. The system proposed in this study achieved a dilution efficiency of approximately 60%, confirming its potential in mitigating such impacts. These findings provide valuable guidance for the development of sustainable and environmentally friendly discharge systems in desalination operations.

articleTitle: Improved Estimation of Photovoltaic Water Pumping System Variables Using a Non-Linear Observer
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study presents an innovative method for estimating the state variables of a photovoltaic pumping system using a nonlinear observer. This approach is based on accurate system modeling and the use of an observer designed via optimization based on linear matrix inequalities (LMI). The observer was used to accurately estimate five key variables: the voltage and current of the photovoltaic array, the current in the DC/DC converter coil, and the voltage and rotational speed of the DC motor. Simulation results, carried out using MATLAB/SIMULINK, show rapid convergence of the estimated variables towards their actual values, even in the presence of variations in climatic conditions, such as irradiance and temperature. The effectiveness of the proposed estimation method is further validated through numerical performance indices, with the root mean square error (RMSE) for the estimated states remaining below 0.005 and a maximum estimation error under 0.45%, ensuring a high estimation accuracy of over 99.55%. This method offers a reliable and cost-effective solution for controlling PV systems by reducing the number of sensors required for single measurements. The performance obtained validates the robustness and efficiency of the proposed observer under different conditions.

articleTitle: Admissibility Analysis for 2-D SRM Continuous Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper investigates the admissibility analysis of a class of two-dimensional singular continuous systems represented by the Roesser model. By transforming the original system into an equivalent separated standard form and applying the Lyapunov method along with specific slack matrices, we propose a technique that avoids singularity issues and establishes sufficient conditions for admissibility in the form of strict linear matrix inequalities. To illustrate the practicality of the proposed approach, we present a simulation example based on a first-order hyperbolic heat equation describing thermal processes.

articleTitle: Simulation of PEM Fuel Cell Stack Performance Under Varying Voltage Conditions Using CFD
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive three-dimensional mathematical model developed to evaluate and simulate the performance of proton exchange membrane fuel cell stack. The study investigates critical parameters, including hydrogen molar fraction distribution, oxygen molar fraction distribution, temperature distribution within the cells, temperature variations in the membrane electrode assemblies, and water activity in the oxygen gas diffusion electrodes under different operating voltages (0.85 V, 0.75 V, 0.65 V, and 0.55 V). Utilizing COMSOL Multiphysics software, the model provides insights into the stack's dynamic behavior across varying conditions. It is found that as the operating voltage decreases, both hydrogen and oxygen consumption increase, leading to higher temperature gradients and more significant water production. These effects are especially pronounced at 0.55 V, where efficient cooling and water management become critical to avoid overheating and water flooding. The results demonstrate that optimal operating conditions are essential for balancing performance and durability, providing valuable data for the design and operation of fuel cell systems in practical applications.

articleTitle: CNN Hyper-parameter Optimization Using Simulated Annealing for MRI Brain Tumor Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Accurate brain tumor classification remains a pivotal challenge in medical imaging, where heterogeneous tumor morphology and subtle anatomical variations complicate diagnostic precision. While Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) serves as the clinical gold standard, manual interpretation of its high-dimensional data can be challenging. Although Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated transformative potential in automating tumor analysis, their efficacy heavily depends on hyper-parameter optimization (HPO). This study introduces a novel integration of Simulated Annealing (SA), a metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by thermodynamic principles, to systematically optimize the hyper-parameters of a CNN for brain tumor classification using MRI images. Our framework incorporates a direct representation of hyperparameters, an efficient perturbation strategy, and a dual evaluation criteria balancing accuracy and model complexity. Experimental results showed that SA applied to CNN hyper-parameter optimization achieved a validation accuracy of 97.25%.

articleTitle: Temperature-dependent variations in donor binding energy in a pillbox quantum dot
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of temperature (T) and dot size (H) on the binding energy (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>) of a shallow donor impurity in a GaAs/Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>As pillbox, enclosed by Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−y</inf>Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>As. Via the variational method (VM) within the effective mass approximation (EMA), the analysis accounts for temperature-dependent changes in the electron effective mass (EEM), dielectric constant (DC), and Conduction band shift. Subband energies are computed using the finite difference method, while E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> of impurity is determined via the VM. Results highlight that T strongly influences the E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>, particularly for smaller quantum dots, with additional dependencies on Aluminum concentration and dot radius. These findings associate with existing literature and donate to a deeper understanding of quantum dot comportment under varying temperature conditions. Additionally, our conclusions are consistent with existing literature and provide meaningful insights into the physical properties of quantum systems under these conditions.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control Combined with Time-Delay Compensation for an Anti-Lock Braking Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this work, we present a Sliding Mode Time Delay Control (SMTDC) approach for regulating the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) in autonomous vehicles. The Sliding Mode Control (SMC) technique is employed to maintain optimal wheel slip, ensuring robust performance against disturbances, uncertainties, and system nonlinearities. A carefully designed sliding surface and control law guarantee finite-time convergence to the sliding manifold. Time Delay Control (TDC) is used to compensate for time lags and delays in the system, which are common in practical applications due to sensor and actuator dynamics. Lyapunov stability theory is used to prove global asymptotic stability. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the (SMTDC) approach in enhancing ABS performance, including wheel slip regulation, braking efficiency, and robustness to disturbances, advancing the safety of autonomous vehicle systems.

articleTitle: Energy of a donor impurity within a quantum dot embedded in a nanorod under an electric field
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: When subjected to an electric field, we theoretically investigate the donor impurity energy, by means of the finite element method in the context of the effective mass approximation. This electronic property is computed for a CdSe quantum dot as a dependence on impurity position and dot size under various electric field strengths. The outcomes show that the single dopant energy reaches a minimum at the center of the quantum dot and decreases significantly as the dot size decreases due to the quantum confinement effect. These findings can be leveraged to enhance electronic devices, particularly those based on doped CdSe/CdS structures.

articleTitle: Digitalisation in Moroccan Institutions: A Catalyst for innovation and transformation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Digital Skills and language learning are essential in the field of law, and the use of educational technologies has become common for enhancing language skills. Moodle and Rosetta Stone are the preferred platforms for the Faculty of Legal, Economic, and Social Sciences at Moulay Ismail University in Meknes, Morocco. This platform is Known for its immersive and interactive approach, so it is crucial to assess its specific effectiveness in the context of Arabic law. The objective of this study is to present the importance of digitalization at Moroccan Institutions, to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the platform, and to propose improvements to optimize the pedagogical effectiveness of digital culture courses and French courses for Arabic Private Law.

articleTitle: High-Performance Biomedical Antenna for Early and Non-Invasive Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This article presents a novel microstrip antenna design for early breast cancer detection, featuring enhanced bandwidth. Designed using HFSS software, the antenna employs edge feeding with a feed line measuring 3.6 mm in length and 3 mm in width. The 70 × 70 mm substrate, with a thickness of 1.6 mm, is fabricated using FR-4 Epoxy, characterized by a relative permittivity of 4.4 and a 50 Ω impedance. The antenna achieves a maximum gain of 4.431 dBi and operates around 2.4 GHz, offering a 100 MHz bandwidth and an average return loss of –32 dB. A breast phantom model with an embedded tumor was developed to evaluate performance, enabling detection based on the specific absorption rate (SAR), which quantifies the energy absorbed by the tissue. The SAR results, peaking at coordinates (0.035, 0.0325, 0.0325), closely align with the tumor's actual location (0, 0, 0). These findings demonstrate the antenna's effectiveness in accurately locating the tumor while adhering to SAR safety standards.

articleTitle: Free vibration analysis of functionally graded plates reinforced with graphene oxide powder
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this research, free vibration analysis of nanocomposite plate reinforced with graphene oxide powder (GOPR) is carried out using an exact analytical approach. So, for the first time the results of the new reinforcement models according to various functionally graded (FG) distributions across the thickness, namely U, X, V and O. The main objective here is to discover the most effective GOP distribution model to improve the vibration behavior of the structure. Moreover, the laws governing the effective material properties of the nanocomposite plate were derived using the Halpin-Tsai micromechanical model. The equations of the studied problem are based on the theory of first order shear deformation. They were developed using Hamilton's principle and solved by an exact analytical approach for a simply supported GOPR nanocomposite plate. Detailed parametric studies are carried out to show the influence of different variables on the natural frequency of nanocomposite plates. The findings of this work reveal that the frequency responses of nanocomposite plates significantly depend on the distribution pattern of GOP.

articleTitle: Comparison of the fundamental topologies of multilevel inverters with two-level inverters for electric vehicle applications: a synthesis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Faced with the growing challenges posed by climate change due to the increase in greenhouse gas emissions, of which the transport sector is one of the main polluters, sustainable solutions are being studied. Electric transport, which is attracting a great deal of interest, offers a solution that will considerably reduce CO2 emissions. Researchers are studying the technologies and improvements to be made to the electric vehicle powertrain and its components, paying increasing attention to power electronics. Advances in power electronics have led to the development of traction inverters. Although current electric vehicles use traditional two-stage inverters, they present certain problems that affect the performance and overall efficiency of the electric vehicle. On the other hand, multilevel inverters offer an interesting solution and are being studied as an alternative to two-level inverters. This paper presents an overview of the most commonly used multilevel inverter topologies, as well as a comparison between the traction inverters used, their advantages and limitations.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking of a Photovoltaic System Using Terminal Sliding mode Controller with a DC to DC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: One essential thing for every photovoltaic generation system, is a maximum power point tracker, in order for the PV system to work properly and give maximum electric energy available. In this manuscript, a PV array supplying a DC load through a DC-to-DC boost converter, controlled by a robust terminal sliding mode MPP controller, is mathematically modeled and numerically simulated in MATLAB environment. To show the robustness and confirm finite time convergence of the TSMC controller the simulations were built upon two weather scenarios, standard test conditions and abrupt changes in temperature and sun radiation. The comparison with integral and conventional sliding modes showed the reliability of the terminal SMC in tracking the MPP in a finite time and effectively, furthermore these results were confirmed through a quantitative evaluation of performance based on the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Influence of hydrostatic pressure and temperature on the electronic properties of doped GaAs/Al0.3Ga0.7As tetrapodal quantum dots
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of quantum confinement and impurity effects in GaAs/Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.3</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.7</inf>As core-shell tetrapodal quantum dots (CSTQDs). Employing finite element method (FEM) and the effective mass approach (EMA), we explore the intricate interplay between nanocrystal geometry, impurity position, barrier composition, and external perturbations such as temperature and hydrostatic pressure. Our findings demonstrate significant tunability of electronic properties, particularly the impurity binding energy (BE), through precise control of these parameters. Building upon the pioneering work of Michael J. Enright et al. (2020) [1] on the epitaxial growth of these unique nanostructures, this research delves into their potential for advanced optoelectronic applications by elucidating the underlying physics of impurity states.

articleTitle: Improved MPPT algorithm for grid-connected PV system
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The grid-connected PV systems (GCPVS) require a high-performing Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm for superior power injection into the grid with minimal losses and reduced Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). Perturb & Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance (INC) are the most popular MPPTs in the field due to their ease of implementation and inferior cost. Still, they suffer from high oscillations, slow response time, and increased THD, leading finally to significant power losses. This paper proposes an improved P&O algorithm to overcome the limitations of conventional MPPTs. A comparative study between the suggested MPPT and P&O algorithm is presented to demonstrate the validity of the proposed control technique.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Biocompatible Ultrasound Sensor for Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Below is the work connected with the development and design of a biocompatible diagnostic device with the basic element a spherical capsule of 1.2 cm in diameter that can operate as an autonomous vibrating system. A piezoelectric ring inside the capsule excites a low resonance frequency, while a network of high frequency sensors allows local scanning. Its hollow structure housed the integration of the active vibration element along with embedded electronics for encoding, control, and analysis. The diagnostic application may require the capsule to operate as a transmitter and receiver simultaneously when configured in a network. This could be a major advantage in medical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Building a Contextualized Arabic Voice Command Corpus for Industrial Automation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Voice command systems are increasingly critical for enhancing human-machine interaction, particularly in industrial environments shaped by Industry 4.0. However, deploying such systems in Arabic-Speaking contexts presents unique challenges due to the morphological complexity of the Arabic language, dialectal variations, and the lack of standardized industrial command corpora. This study addresses these gaps by introducing a specialized Arabic voice command corpus tailored for industrial applications. Data was collected from major stakeholders in sectors such as energy production, railway operations, and chemical processing, culminating in a corpus of 35 distinct commands. A comprehensive syllabic analysis revealed dominant patterns in CV and CVC structures, essential for optimizing speech recognition systems. Cross-Sector validation was conducted with industry professionals from prominent Moroccan organizations, including ONE, ONCF, and OCP, ensuring alignment with real-world operational requirements. The resulting corpus covers critical industrial functions such as process control, safety protocols, maintenance, and inventory management. By integrating linguistic insights with practical applications, this research lays the groundwork for developing robust, context-aware Arabic automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. The study contributes to the advancement of Arabic natural language processing and enhances accessibility to Industry 4.0 technologies in Arabic-Speaking regions.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis: Dissecting A Decade of Research on Green Technology, Dynamic Capabilities, and Sustainability Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study employs a bibliometric approach to examine the evolution of research on green technology, dynamic capabilities, and sustainability performance over the past decade. By analyzing 722 publications indexed in the Scopus database from 2014 to 2024, the study uncovers major trends, influential publications, and collaboration patterns within this field. The analysis also maps out the contributions of various countries, with China, the United States, and Spain emerging as leading contributors. Additionally, the research identifies leading journals and authors shaping the discourse, shedding light on the field’s intellectual foundations. The findings underscore the importance of further investigating how dynamic capabilities drive green innovation and sustainable practices across diverse settings. Ultimately, these insights offer valuable directions for future research and practical efforts to enhance sustainability outcomes.

articleTitle: Hyperledger Fabric Smart Contract Security: Risks and Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Smart contracts, self-executing programs deployed on blockchain networks, offer significant benefits in terms of transparency, efficiency, and trustless operations. However, their widespread adoption is hindered by security vulnerabilities that can lead to financial losses and operational failures. These vulnerabilities often stem from coding errors and logical flaws, such as input validation issues, race conditions, and value propagation problems. In this work, we propose a systematic analysis of common security risks in smart contracts, based on an in-depth literature review and the examination of several case studies. The results identify the most critical vulnerabilities and suggest best practices to mitigate these risks. For instance, the study highlights the importance of rigorous input validation and the use of formal models to verify contract logic. In short, this study provides valuable guidelines for smart contract developers and contributes to strengthening the security of blockchain applications. As a perspective for future work, avenues for research on the formalization of smart contracts and the automation of security testing will be explored.

articleTitle: LPV-Based Sliding Mode Control with Varying Longitudinal Velocity
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation study of a sliding mode control (SMC) scheme for a vehicle lateral dynamics system under longitudinal velocity variations, modeled as a Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) system. The longitudinal velocity, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, varies in three distinct functions: constant, sinusoidal, and ramp-up. The proposed control strategy ensures robustness and adaptability to dynamic changes in V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, demonstrating its effectiveness in uncertain environments with varying vehicle behaviors. Performance metrics, including lateral error, control effort, settling time, and energy consumption, are analyzed. Comparative insights highlight the benefits of the LPV-based SMC design in handling disturbances and parameter uncertainties.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of Empirical Models for Forecasting Photovoltaic Power Output: An Update and Case Study in Tangier, Morocco
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of eighteen empirical models commonly used for predicting photovoltaic (PV) power output. These models were thoroughly validated, and their accuracy was carefully assessed using experimental data from the PV installation at the Faculty of Science and Technology in Tangier, Morocco. The results demonstrate a strong correlation between the measured and predicted values, confirming the overall reliability of the models. Among them, the model developed by Sandia National Laboratories [1] proved to be the most suitable, delivering the most accurate power output predictions across various climatic conditions, with a normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) of approximately 7.112% during the six-month monitoring period. This outstanding performance emphasizes the model's robustness and applicability in different weather scenarios. The research not only highlights the effectiveness of the Sandia model but also provides valuable insights into the comparative performance of various empirical models, offering guidance in selecting the best tools for PV power forecasting.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a Dual-Polarized U-Shaped Aperture Antenna Using Metamaterial-Embedded Aluminum Plane for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact, high-gain dual-polarized U-shaped aperture antenna designed for 5G communication systems, highlighting the impact of a metamaterial-embedded aluminum plane placed beneath the lower substrate. Dual polarization is achieved through two U-shaped apertures, which also improve impedance matching and coupling efficiency. The antenna is built using two substrates separated by an air gap, with orthogonal feed lines below the lower substrate powering a square radiating element situated beneath the upper substrate. The U-shaped apertures, etched into the ground plane above the lower substrate, facilitate efficient coupling of electromagnetic waves. Thanks to the integration of the metamaterial (MTM)-embedded aluminum plane, the antenna exhibits a significant performance boost: the operational bandwidth is extended from 500 MHz to over 800 MHz, the inter-port isolation improves from 26 dB to over 32 dB, the realized gain increases from 6.27 dBi to 9.35 dBi, and the radiation efficiency improves from 77% to over 90%. Simulation results show that the metamaterial-patterned aluminum plane significantly enhances the antenna’s gain by almost 3 dB, while the design also demonstrates excellent port isolation and over 90% radiation efficiency. All design and simulation steps were carried out using both CST and HFSS software, and RO4003C was chosen as the substrate material (thickness: 0.813 mm, dielectric constant: 3.5).

articleTitle: The dual effect of Ellis model and Biot number on the Darcy-Benard instability: A numerical study
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The study examines the dual behavior of the Biot number and the Ellis number on the Darcy-Benard convective instability problem saturated with a shear-thinning fluid whose behavior appertains to the Ellis model. The dimensionless process is carried out, which leads to the appearance of various governing parameters among them the Biot number and the Ellis number. Asymmetric thermal conditions are assumed by considering the Robin condition at the lower impermeable layer and the Dirichlet condition at the upper one. A numerical technique is employed in Mathematica 10 to handle the eigenvalues problem developed by the linear stability analysis. Based on the results, the transverse modes exhibit the highest level of instability. Furthermore, compared to the Newtonian fluid, the shear-thinning fluid illustrates unstable behavior for the same flow configuration.

articleTitle: Defect Mode Properties in a 1D Acoustic System Based on Closed Serial Resonators
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study investigates the complex dynamics of waveguides by analyzing periodic structures incorporating closed resonators. We have examined a specific configuration composed of N single resonators, with and without geometrical defects in the main waveguide. The approach adopted is based on the transfer matrix method, enabling detailed analysis of the defect impact and complete characterization of low-frequency resonance phenomena. Under optimal conditions, the structural periodicity of the system leads to the creation of an acoustic band gap where the wave cannot propagate in the structure. Moreover, the presence of a defect has a significant effect on the appearance of localized modes in the acoustic band gap. Increasing the defect guide leads to the generation of multiple resonant modes with high acoustic transmittance. The position of these modes was well controlled by varying the length of the defect. These results are very useful in the field of acoustics, and pave the way for innovative applications such as acoustic filters and high-resolution sensors. This study thus offers an innovative framework for exploiting the effects of defects in waveguide systems, contributing to the evolution of modern acoustic technologies.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization Tool for Electric Vehicle Autonomy
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The suggested method entails introducing the design of a computer tool that enables the modeling of the electric vehicle power chain in the first stage. A library created using the Matlab-Simulink environment serves as the foundation for this phase. This library contains all of the chain’s components and provides multiple configurations for each one. The tool resolves the autonomy optimization issue in the second stage. A program that uses genetic algorithms resolves this issue. In order to maximize autonomy, the program optimizes the parameters of a chain’s configuration that the designer has selected. A graphical user interface created in the Matlab environment serves as the foundation for the utility.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Sliding Mode Controller for Three-Phase Single-Stage Grid-Tied Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: A nonlinear sliding mode control (SMC) strategy is proposed in this paper for a three-phase, single-stage, grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) system. The controlled system consists of a photovoltaic generator (PVG), a three-phase voltage source inverter, a grid filter, and a balanced three-phase electrical grid. The controller seeks to accomplish three key objectives: (1) maximize power extraction from the PVG; (2) sustain a unity power factor on the grid side; and (3) guarantee the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. A sliding mode control technique is applied to the nonlinear system model formulated in the d-q synchronous reference frame. Theoretical stability analysis and simulation outcomes provide strong validation that the proposed control strategy effectively fulfills all predefined objectives.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Parabolic Trough Collector Receiver with Two different Pipe Exchangers
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this work, a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis is conducted to investigate the parabolic trough collector (PTC) receiver with two different tube exchangers: one with a U-shaped tube and another with a UU-shaped tube. The outlet temperature, the thermal efficiency, and the temperature gaps are analyzed for three mass flow rates and an inlet temperature. The highest outlet temperature is recorded for the lowest mass flow rate, and the UU configuration outperforms the U configuration with an enhancement of 1.8% in terms of outlet temperature. The highest value of thermal efficiency is achieved for the highest mass flow rate, with values of 75.5% and 65.2% for the UU configuration and the U configuration, respectively. Concerning the overall receiver temperature difference, the UU configuration showed a significant reduction of temperature gaps compared to the U configuration for all simulated mass flow rates. The findings revealed that the use of different shapes of the exchanger has the ability to improve the PTC systems’ performances.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control Strategy of Wind Turbine System Connected to the Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The integration of renewable energies into modern power grids poses a number of challenges, not least the control of wind turbines to ensure the stability and efficiency of power grids. This article presents three advanced control strategies for grid-connected wind turbines, based on nonlinear control, including backstepping, sliding mode and PI control.After describing system modeling, robust control methods are developed. The outcomes of the simulation show that the suggested tactics can keep the system stable even when wind and grid disturbances occur. This study emphasizes how crucial optimal management is to enhancing the integration of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: ’Ignore All and Accept My Resume’: The Impact of Prompt Injection in Automatic Resume Screening
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Users of generative AI models—such as ChatGPT, Claude, or any other model—are becoming familiar with prompt manipulation, contributing to the Prompt Engineering as an emerging technical field. Indeed, every new technology possesses a dual nature and can be able of being exploited for both beneficial and harmful purposes. The harmful aspect in the field of prompt engineering is known as Prompt Injection. The latter, which is a harmful practice used in different situations, involves manipulating AI systems by injecting malicious instructions. In the context of resume screening, job candidates often exploit this technique to manipulate the applicant tracking system (ATS) by inserting a harmful prompt into the resume to be approved. By examining recent studies, this review seeks to understand this new area of concern by examining the influence of prompt injection on resume screening. The topic is still general and not tailored to a specific use case, such as resume screening, owing to its novelty. Therefore, we provide an overview to shed light on how this could affect the quality of the hiring decisions.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Moroccan Primary Arabic Textbooks
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Vocabulary is the fundamental element of any linguistic corpus, directly reflecting the language used in a given context. A corpus must be representative of the language it aims to model. A diverse and rich vocabulary contributes to the quality of language models. School textbooks are a valuable source for creating corpora, as they offer a glimpse into the language taught, the topics covered, and the target language level. Analysing the vocabulary in these textbooks can help identify both the strengths and weaknesses in teaching materials and develop new language learning tools. This study aims to evaluate Moroccan primary Arabic textbooks, compiled in the MoSAR (Modern Standard Arabic Readability) corpus, and to utilize the various versions of this corpus to create an enhanced and optimized version.

articleTitle: Mold Flow Analysis of Panel Mount Connector: PPO vs. PBT for Performance Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Plastics, initially viewed as alternatives to metals and wood, have become indispensable due to their versatility and customizable properties. However, optimizing the injection molding process for high-performance applications remains a significant challenge, particularly in managing defects such as warping, shrinkage, and deformation. These issues arise from the complex interplay of material properties and process parameters, necessitating advanced modeling and simulation to address them effectively. This study examines the mold flow behavior of a high-performance circular panel mount connector, comparing polyphenylene oxide (PPO) and polybutylene terephthalate (PBT). By simulating both materials on the same model, we analyze their impact on fill patterns, shrinkage, warping, and deformation. The quantitative results indicate that PPO exhibits a lower maximum volumetric shrinkage (12%) compared to PBT (15%) in Moldex3D simulations, highlighting its superior dimensional stability and reduced risk of warpage. The proposed solution involves leveraging accurate Computer-Aided Engineering (CAE) simulations to identify optimal material and process configurations. The main contributions of this work are threefold: first, a comparative analysis of PPO and PBT to determine their suitability for high-precision applications; second, the identification of key parameters influencing defect formation and strategies for their mitigation; and third, the demonstration of the critical role of simulation in enhancing material selection and process efficiency. The findings offer valuable insights into optimizing injection molding for industrial applications, underscoring the importance of simulation as a vital tool in advancing the quality and performance of polymer-based components.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Grey Wolf Optimizer and P&O MPPT for PV Systems under Shading
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: MPPT techniques are fundamental for boosting the efficiency of photovoltaic arrays under varying climatic situations. This work evaluates the performance of the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) strategy, and the classic Perturb and Observe (P&O) technique with step sizes of 0.001 and 0.008 in partially shaded PV systems, where shading complicates the tracking process by introducing multiple local maxima. We use MATLAB/Simulink environment to model and simulate the system using different controllers. Simulation results indicate that the GWO strategy identifies the global maximum power point (GMPP) with higher accuracy and effectiveness under dynamic shading conditions and temperature variations. In contrast, the performance of the P&O strategy is highly related to the chosen step size, which should be selected optimally to balance accuracy, stability, and convergence time. In conclusion, GWO is confirmed to be a more robust and reliable method than P&O, with higher efficiency, especially in challenging irradiance scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of Classical and Adaptive Control Systems for Pitch Angle and Altitude Tracking in Aircraft Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to the design and implementation of advanced flight control systems aimed at achieving precise altitude and pitch angle regulation for aerial vehicles. I develop a classical control framework that integrates feedback mechanisms utilizing critical state variables, including angle of attack, pitch rate, and integral error states, to ensure effective control over the vehicle’s dynamics. To stabilize the inner-loop pitch angle dynamics, I employ a compensator designed through root locus analysis. This approach facilitates the attainment of desired stability margins and control performance metrics, thereby enhancing the responsiveness of the system to perturbations. Following this, I address the outer-loop altitude tracking system, which is similarly closed using a compensator design. This section of the system encounters challenges related to the characteristics of a double integrator and the presence of unstable zeros, necessitating a robust control strategy. In addition to the classical control design, I introduce an adaptive control framework to manage uncertainties inherent in system stability and control derivatives effectively. This adaptive architecture employs a model reference approach, enabling the system to dynamically adjust to variations and uncertainties while tracking the desired commands. The adaptive mechanism is grounded in Lyapunov-based methods, which are employed to ensure global stability throughout the control process. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the efficacy of both the classical and adaptive control strategies. The results indicate that the proposed methodologies successfully achieve stable altitude tracking and robust performance in the presence of various system uncertainties. The findings contribute to the broader field of flight control systems, providing insights into the integration of classical and adaptive techniques for enhanced aerial vehicle performance.

articleTitle: Feature extraction using partial overlapping block-based reconstruction with exact continuous moments: Legendre and Gegenbauer
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced algorithm for pattern recognition using an partial overlapping method of a 4x4 block and exact computation moments: Legendre and Gegenbauer. By employing a limited number of moments (order 0), the methods achieve high accuracy while maintaining a low computational cost. It also provides better recognition rates compared to conventional methods based on calculating moments on the entire image, which involve higher orders. Experimental results highlights the superior performance of the proposed method, particularly with Legendre moments, compared to existing techniques.

articleTitle: Performance Validation of a Three-Phase NPC Three-Level Inverter using a Novel Sinusoidal PWM technique for Induction Motor Scalar Control
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Multilevel inverters have become essential tools in the field of electric energy conversion for both industrial environments and transportation. The performance provided by these converters, particularly in terms of efficiency and the quality of generated electrical signals, has secured them a prominent place in traction applications using asynchronous motors. This document aims to study the performance of an asynchronous motor controlled through a three-phase NPC three-level inverter using a novel modulation technique compared to a two-level inverter. Simulation results are validated using MATLAB/Simulink, while experimental results are obtained using a DSP card for control signal

articleTitle: SchedAI: An AI-Driven Faculty Preference-Based Scheduler
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The university faced significant challenges in creating a time schedule for the college departments of Western Mindanao State University (WMSU), relying on a traditional manual method that required incorporating various requirements and constraints. This process was time-consuming, prone to errors, and could take anywhere from a day to a week to complete. To address these issues, “SchedAI” was developed to automate the scheduling process using a backtracking algorithm. Designed for efficiency, “SchedAI” simplifies scheduling by integrating faculty preferences and institutional constraints, enabling the quick creation of dynamic and conflict-free schedules. Benchmark tests show that while the greedy algorithm is faster, it often generates overlapping schedules, whereas the backtracking algorithm produces schedules with zero conflicts. The system was evaluated based on functionality, usability, and reliability through quantitative data collection from faculty members. Results showed an average faculty satisfaction rating of 3.37, indicating positive performance while highlighting areas for improvement. Future enhancements may include integrating blockchain technology for security, considering student preferences, generating multiple scheduling options, and implementing a SMART scheduling system. “SchedAI” marks a significant step toward modernizing scheduling at WMSU by reducing administrative workload, minimizing errors, improving stakeholder satisfaction, and paving the way for future technological advancements in educational administration.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Induction Machines Fault Using Vibration-Based Analysis under COMSOL Multiphysics within a Preventive Maintenance Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, a predictive maintenance strategy is developed to enhance the fault identification of induction machines using the analysis of residual mechanical vibrations. Induction machines are the most widely adopted machines in many industrial environments, owing to their high robustness, simplicity and economic efficiency. Nevertheless, these machines are susceptible to both electrical and mechanical failures, including stator phase deficiencies, which may result in significant downtime and expensive maintenance charges. The approach developed is designed by combining FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) and vibration signal analysis to detect faults at an early stage. The methodology has been validated by simulations performed with COMSOL Multiphysics. The results reveal a significant improvement over traditional maintenance methods based solely on vibration analysis in the early detection of failures, resulting in reduced downtime and lower maintenance costs.

articleTitle: Privacy in Focus: The Role of Accessible Language and Interface Design in Users' Perceptions of Data Protection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Although traditional privacy policies are the most common resource for communicating to data subjects about the collection and processing of personal information, these texts are often long and difficult for users to understand. The aim of this article is to analyze how the accessibility and clarity of information on data protection policies in software interfaces influences users' perceptions of privacy through a literature review. As a result, the methods investigated proved to be potential factors that increase data subjects' understanding of privacy policies and, consequently, increase the assertiveness of choices in the act of informed consent.

articleTitle: Improved Nonlinear Control and Efficient Energy Flow Management in a Low-voltage AC Microgrid integrating Wind turbine, PV and Battery Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents an improved nonlinear control strategy and efficient energy flow management in a low-voltage AC microgrid integrating a wind turbine, a photovoltaic system and an energy storage battery. The AC microgrid is designed to operate in a grid-connected configuration, ensuring optimal energy production, storage and consumption. In this context, a mathematical model of the overall system has been developed and backstepping controllers have been synthesized to achieve the control objectives. The convergence of closed-loop control is formally analyzed using Lyapunov stability theory. A new algorithm is proposed to maximize energy extraction from renewable sources while simultaneously managing battery storage for optimal performance and reliability. The approach also ensures grid stability through efficient power factor correction (PFC) and load balancing. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controllers in meeting control objectives, illustrating improvements in energy efficiency, stability and overall system performance under varying load and environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Towards a new data transmission model for smart farms
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In today's world, smart farming has become a necessity in the light of climate change and demographic evolution. With the emergence of the term Smart Farm, this goal has become increasingly achievable. The use of the Internet of Things and artificial intelligence technologies has enabled great strides to be made with promising results in terms of increasing productivity while minimizing the use of natural resources. In this context, a number of studies have taken advantage of new technologies to propose intelligent irrigation scheduling systems, but taking into consideration only soil water properties as a basis of their research. A recently published study has shown that good agricultural management must take into account the climatic, physical, chemical, biological and hydrological properties of a crop field, and has shown that the detection of each property is possible through the use of new technologies. Based on this research, in this article we have proposed a new conceptual model for data transmission in a smart farm. The proposed model combines the use of Internet of Things technologies, artificial intelligence and intelligent agents to enable holistic, real-time, sustainable and efficient farm management. The results found in this article have also helped to shed light on several lines of research and thus open the way for further studies.

articleTitle: Structural damage detection of wind turbine based on YOLO11
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Conventional methods for visually examining wind turbines have numerous constraints and frequently fall short of guaranteeing optimal outcomes. Flaws or impairments on wind turbine blades diminish the lifespan and energy production efficiency of the turbine, while also escalating monitoring inaccuracies, safety hazards, and maintenance expenses. The automated assessment of wind turbines via deep learning has become a powerful and efficient method for tackling quality control challenges in the industrial sector, particularly through object detection methods using the YOLO versions that improves the detection of minor objects. Consequently, this research suggests identifying wind turbine faults through the latest version of YOLO (YOLO11) lightweight model that was released in 2024, which includes enhancements in YOLO’s series network effectiveness, precision, and real-time object detection features. YOLO11 incorporates an improved backbone and neck architecture, introducing components like the C3k2 (Cross Stage Partial with kernel size 2) block, SPPF (Spatial Pyramid Pooling - Fast), and C2PSA (Convolutional block with Parallel Spatial Attention), which enhance feature extraction and lead to higher precision, allowing the model to achieve better computational efficiency without compromising accuracy. Defect detection on wind turbines is challenging because there is a high similarity between the defects and the structure itself, but also the very small size of the defects on the structure may not be detected. Through the results obtained but also by comparing our findings with the studies already done, in this article we have demonstrated that YOLO11 is capable of detecting several defects at the same time with precision. In consequence our model can assist in improving wind turbines inspection.

articleTitle: Enhanced Drowsiness Prediction through a Fusion of ANFIS and BLSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study proposes an innovative hybrid model to detect driver drowsiness by integrating an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BLSTM) network. Given that drowsiness is a critical factor in road accidents, the development of accurate and efficient detection systems is essential for improving traffic safety. ANFIS demonstrates a rapid convergence within just 20 iterations, effectively addressing nonlinearities and uncertainties in behavioral data. BLSTM complements this by capturing complex temporal dependencies in both directions, achieving an accuracy of 98.48% and an F1 score of 0.985507. The fusion of these models further enhances performance, with the hybrid ANFIS-BLSTM model achieving a remarkable accuracy of 98.46% and reducing the mean squared error (MSE) to 0.019896. These results confirm the model’s ability to provide a robust and reliable solution for real-time drowsiness detection, ultimately contributing to safer driving conditions.

articleTitle: Assessing User Experience in Academic Information Systems: Insights from Heuristic Evaluation and UEQ
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The website of the Atma Jaya Yogyakarta University Academic Information System (SIKMA UAJY) helps students complete tasks such as class registration, JOGIS, counseling, and SPAMA independently. Based on interviews, UAJY students using SIKMA felt the need for a user experience evaluation. Identified issues include the lack of feedback when uploading SPAMA, a rigid user interface, an empty main dashboard, and several user-interface elements that need improvement. This study employs the heuristic evaluation method (HE) with three expert UI/UX evaluators and the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) to assess user experience and provide improvement recommendations for the SIKMA UAJY website. The UEQ evaluation results showed below average scores in attractiveness, perspicuity, efficiency, and dependability, and poor scores in stimulation and novelty. The HE method identified 56 issues, summarized into 35 key problems. After implementing the improvement recommendations, a reanalysis of the user experience showed higher scores, achieving good ratings in all aspects. These evaluations and improvements are designed to improve the user experience of the SIKMA UAJY website.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Adding Two Reflectors for Different Solar Cooker Geometries
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The use of renewable energy, which is naturally inexhaustible, has seen significant growth in recent years. It plays a crucial role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and contributes to the global fight against climate change. Solar concentration technologies, which produce heat and electricity without relying on fossil fuels or generating polluting emissions, are driving a transition toward the use of solar, wind, and hydro energy. Among the methods that directly utilize solar energy are solar cookers, which capture and concentrate sunlight to generate heat. In this study, an optical simulation was conducted to analyze the distribution of solar rays on absorbers with different solar cooker geometries. The aim was to evaluate the effect of adding reflectors on solar ray concentration across various days of the year. Two reflectors were considered in this study: a primary reflector and a secondary one. The results indicate that using a primary reflector provides better ray concentration compared to a secondary reflector when applied to the front wall of the cookers, regardless of the selected geometries.

articleTitle: Forecasting electric vehicles recharge impact on distribution network
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The expansion of the electric vehicles market has resulted in the major emergence of new models with increasingly efficient charging systems, designed to meet drivers' everyday needs. This emergence will undoubtedly result in the proliferation of electric vehicle charging stations that will be connected to the electrical distribution network for medium voltage power. In this paper, we have demonstrated the impact of fast charging of electric vehicles during peak periods exceeding the power limit of the distribution network compared to random charging. Additionally, two artificial intelligence models, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Random Forest (RF), were used to predict potential power surges resulting from electric vehicle fast charging. The prediction results show high performance for the RF model compared to those obtained by ANN model.

articleTitle: Context-based Word Definition Classification for Arabic: Leveraging Pre-trained Language Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research addresses the challenge of context-based word definition classification, a critical task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for morphologically rich languages like Arabic. Using a dataset of 3,670 annotated examples, we propose a methodology combining pre-trained BERT embeddings with cosine similarity to evaluate the contextual alignment of ambiguous word senses. Our approach achieved 80% accuracy, outperforming traditional methods like Word2Vec and Lesk by a significant margin. These findings highlight the potential of pre-trained transformers for tasks such as machine translation, information retrieval, and conversational AI in low-resource languages. Limitations include computational demands and limited gloss coverage, which will be addressed in future work by expanding resources and refining classification techniques for dialectal and multi-lingual scenarios.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Moodle Adoption at a Libyan University Using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study explored and evaluated the effectiveness of variables influencing students’ use of Moodle (e-learning management system) based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) at the Libyan International Medical University (LIMU) in Benghazi. Additionally, this study aimed to identify correlations between variables affecting successful Moodle adoption, specifically perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and behavioral intention based on the TAM. Using a descriptive-analytical approach with a sample of 328 students, the results revealed that perceived ease of use was strongly correlated with perceived usefulness in a statistically significant direct relationship. The findings also demonstrated that perceived usefulness had a positive and statistically significant direct relationship with behavioral intention to use Moodle. Furthermore, a positive and statistically significant correlation was found between perceived ease of use and behavioral intention. These results confirm that both perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness are positively associated with behavioral intention to use Moodle.

articleTitle: Enhancing Distance Learning in African Universities: A Moodle Plugin for Personalized Support and Improved Engagement
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Faced with growing enrolments, a shortage of teaching staff and limited capacity, African universities are struggling to manage access to higher education, particularly in Senegal. Distance learning appears to be an essential solution to these challenges of massification and unequal access. However, distance learning platforms face a number of obstacles, such as the absence of personalized feedback, the lack of teacher time for individualized support, and students' difficulties in identifying relevant pedagogical resources. To overcome these limitations, we developed a Moodle plugin to integrate a detailed dashboard. This enables students to track their performance, access personalized recommendations, and teachers to automatically analyze assessments to detect trends and difficulties. A student feedback system has also been implemented, using Asterisk to launch automatic calls to students experiencing difficulties. This solution aims to improve efficiency and engagement in distance learning. Our future work focuses on Reducing university drop-outs through smart contract.

articleTitle: Harnessing Kernel Tricks for Nonlinear Problem Solving: SVM Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Real-world problems often exhibit complex, nonlinear relationships between variables, which cannot be adequately addressed through linear assumptions. This paper explores how advanced algorithms, specifically the kernel trick, transform these nonlinear problems into higher-dimensional spaces, facilitating easier solutions. The mathematical underpinnings of the kernel trick, including the Volterra filter and Hilbert space transformations, are explored. The study implements Support Vector Machines (SVM) with Gaussian kernels to solve the XOR Toy problem, double Fibonacci spiral, and the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset, highlighting the efficacy of nonlinear transformations. Experimental results demonstrate high classification accuracy, validating the robust application of kernel methods in complex data analysis.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Noise Amplifier using a Chebyshev-Type Bandpass Coupled Resonator Filter with Distributed Elements from 2 GHz to 3 GHz
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this work, we present the design and implementation of a low-noise amplifier (LNA) incorporating coupled resonator band-pass filters at the input and output stages. To design this amplifier, we used the pseudomorphic HEMT RF transistor ATF-34143. The results show that the modeled LNA is unconditionally stable across the entire frequency band [2–3] GHz. Furthermore, it offers a maximum gain of up to 17 dB, with a noise figure (NFmin) not exceeding 2.29 dB, and low input and output reflection coefficients (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf>), which remain below -10 dB across the entire band. The use of distributed elements, such as the coupled resonator filter, simplifies the manufacturing process and reduces costs, requiring only a localized stability resistor. This cost-effective and efficient design makes the modeled LNA suitable for various applications, including wireless communications, the Internet of Things (IoT), telemetry systems, and remote monitoring.

articleTitle: Simulated Annealing-Based Energy and Traffic-Aware Virtual Machine Placement in Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The fast expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) is resulting in an unprecedented rise in data output, necessitating significant computer resources for processing and analysis. Fog computing (FC) complements cloud computing by bringing data processing closer to IoT devices, lowering network congestion, and improving system responsiveness. However, effective resource management, particularly virtual machine placement (VMP), remains a substantial difficulty in fog environments. This study looks at the power consumption of fog computing systems, specifically how VMP methods affect server and network energy usage. A simulated annealing-based VMP approach is suggested to optimize VM allocation across physical machines (PMs), reduce overall power consumption, and improve network traffic efficiency. A comparison of three VM allocation rules (LFF, MFF, and EnergyNetAware<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-SA) reveals that EnergyNetAware<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-SA consumes the least amount of energy across different workloads, outperforming previous techniques. It delivers up to 10% lower server power usage than LFF and 29% lower than MFF, while decreasing network power consumption by up to 20% and 33%, respectively. Furthermore, total power consumption is lowered by up to 14% versus LFF and 29% versus MFF.

articleTitle: Evolution of Hospital Waste Management Practices: Past, current state, and future perspectives
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Disposal of hospital waste is critical for protecting public health and the environment. This article focuses on analysis using RStudio and VOSviewer to examine trends in advanced technologies and sustainability initiatives. However, beyond technological advancements, the study also highlights significant challenges related to organizational inefficiencies, governance issues, environmental impacts, and infectious waste disposal. Addressing these challenges requires not only technological innovations but also policy reforms and enhanced regulatory frameworks. This study underlines the need for a comprehensive, collaborative approach and recommends the adoption of robust methods to improve the efficiency and safety of waste management practices.

articleTitle: User Experience Analysis on Geek Academy Website as Job Training Institution Using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) and Usability Testing Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: LPK Geek Academy, established in 2022 and approved by the Ministry of Manpower (KEMNAKER), provides flexible online training to help the workforce acquire industry-aligned skills with digital certification. Therefore, Geek Academy's website was created to assist the workforce in gaining flexible online training, helping them develop skills with digital certification that align with industry requirements. This study evaluates the user experience (UX) and usability of the Geek Academy website to improve user satisfaction and the reputation of its training services. Conducted in November 2024 with 67 active users, the research employed the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) to assess six UX dimensions: attractiveness, perspicuity, efficiency, dependability, stimulation, and novelty. Usability Testing was also used to evaluate functional aspects of the website. The analysis revealed low-quality ratings across all UX dimensions, ranking in the bottom 25% of the UEQ benchmark. However, usability testing showed that the website functioned adequately, allowing users to complete tasks. Overall, users had a negative perception of the website. Based on these findings, the study recommends improving the website's interface design, enhancing emotional appeal, and optimizing navigation to boost user satisfaction and service quality.

articleTitle: Modeling in Industry 4.0: Key Tools and Techniques for Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The advent of Industry 4.0 has revolutionized production and maintenance systems, driving unprecedented levels of efficiency, sustainability, and reliability. However, this review also considers the evolving landscape with the emergence of Industry 5.0, where human ingenuity and machine capabilities collaborate more seamlessly. This review examines the transformative tools and technologies integral to Industry 4.0, including digital twins, federated learning, agent AI, and cyber-physical systems. By synthesizing insights from peer-reviewed articles, technical reports, and case studies, the study provides a comprehensive exploration of these advanced methodologies, emphasizing their practical applications in intelligent manufacturing. The analysis highlights the significant benefits— such as enhanced operational performance, predictive maintenance, and real-time decision-making—while addressing challenges like data privacy, computational demands, and system scalability. It offers insights into solutions that can pave the way for smoother transitions into Industry 5.0. The findings aim to establish a foundation for the development of innovative, adaptive models tailored to the dynamic, interconnected ecosystems of Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Graph embeddings vs. Contextual embeddings: An efficient approach to Arabic sentiment analysis for improving decision making in business intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The analyze of people’s opinions, feelings, and attitudes has a significant impact across various application domains, such as business intelligence, where it helps improve company services, enhance marketing strategies, and support better decision making. In recent years, sentiment analysis in the Arabic language has become increasingly challenging due to its status as one of the most widely spoken languages and its complex linguistic characteristics.In this research, we propose a novel comparative study of two efficient feature extraction approaches applied to an Arabic dataset, which include the graph embedding-based approach utilizing DeepWalk and Node2Vec techniques and the contextual embedding-based approach leveraging AraBERT. The embeddings generated by these methods are trained using various machine learning and deep learning algorithms, such as Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVM), stacking ensemble classifiers (EC), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP).Additionally, the AraBERT model is employed as a classifier. The performance of the models is evaluated using multiple metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC curve, Cohen's kappa, and a novel metric assessing the time required to generate embeddings. The results indicate that the contextual embeddings approach, particularly when combined with the AraBERT classifier and Bi-LSTM, demonstrates superior performance across all evaluation metrics. This highlights the effectiveness of contextual embeddings in capturing semantic relationships between words, outperforming the graph embedding approach.

articleTitle: Mapping AI Research in North Africa: A Bibliometric Analysis for Trends and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The rapid advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) offer transformative opportunities to address global challenges. For North African countries, sharing common contexts and facing compounded challenges from climate change and resource limitations, AI provides a unique opportunity for North African countries to overcome scientific and technological barriers, potentially narrowing the gap with global leaders.By analysing Scopus data, this bibliometric study reveals that AI research is a dynamic and rapidly evolving field, with 61% of publications appearing since 2019. Focusing on the 2019-2024 period and the dominant publication types, the analysis identifies 1.6 million publications, heavily concentrated in "Computer Science" (62%), "Engineering" (42%), and "Mathematics" (20%), reflecting both the foundational development of the discipline and its expanding application across diverse fields. A few countries also dominate AI research, with China, the USA, and India collectively accounting for over 60% of publications. North African countries have a modest presence, led by Egypt (0.8% of global publications, ranked 28th), followed by Morocco (0.6%, 39th), Algeria (0.4%, 49th), Tunisia (0.4%, 50th), and Libya (0.03%, 92nd). SciVal analysis reveals key disparities in AI research outputs, collaboration patterns, and thematic priorities across North African countries. Egypt excels in collaboration, patent citations, and impactful contributions to global topics, particularly in materials science, energy, and medicine, reflecting its strong AI focus. Morocco shows dynamism in decision sciences, agriculture, and management, emphasising sustainable growth, but struggles with limited collaboration and industrial ties. Algeria benefits from international and industrial partnerships for prioritising materials science, energy, and earth sciences, reflecting industrial and environmental goals. Tunisia, despite similar output, has scattered contributions and demonstrates specialisation in molecular biology, social sciences, and medicine, with notable transfer to industry. Though low output, Libya benefits from advanced collaborations and focuses on mathematics and decision sciences, focusing on academic bases of AI. These disparities in AI research outputs and strategic orientations highlight the need for targeted regional cooperation. North African countries could establish collaborative research networks that leverage their collective strengths in areas like renewable energy, agriculture, and e-learning. Policy frameworks should focus on fostering cross-border partnerships, encouraging joint ventures between academia, industry, and government, and promoting AI collaboration in priority sectors such as climate change and resource management. Additionally, Egypt's leadership in AI could serve as a model for scaling up efforts in other countries. Morocco's growing expertise in sustainable development presents an opportunity for deeper collaboration in decision sciences and management. By aligning AI efforts with shared regional challenges, such as climate change, North African countries can create a more integrated and resilient research ecosystem, fostering innovation that benefits the whole region.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection Approach Based on VGG16 and Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has become an invaluable tool in various fields, especially in medicine, where it significantly aids in disease detection. Early detection of brain tumors is critical for improving patient survival rates and optimizing therapeutic strategies. In this study, we propose an approach based on the pre-trained VGG16 model, leveraging transfer learning to identify the presence of tumors in brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans. The dataset used, Brain MRI Images for Brain Tumor Detection, provides a diverse range of images that support robust and relevant model training. A fine-tuning phase was incorporated to tailor the model to the specificities of medical data. Experimental results demonstrate an accuracy exceeding 86%, highlighting the effectiveness of this proposed approach for automated brain tumor detection.This study paves the way for promising prospects, particularly in terms of methodological improvements and deployment in real clinical settings.

articleTitle: Optimized Clustering Approach for WSN Using WCLUST Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things applications has resulted in easy device integration in Wireless Sensor Networks, enabling real-time data collection and coordination. However, seamless integration is still plagued by issues such as energy constraints and high energy consumption due to inefficient data communication. Many studies explored clustering methods to address such issues. Here, we introduce the Whale-Based Algorithm for cluster establishment and a Selection Factor for Cluster Head selection—key steps that minimize paths and save energy. With the use of the proposed method, our approach improves clustering quality with the establishment of dense and energy-saving clusters. The Selection Factor provides dynamic selection of the most suitable Cluster Heads according to residual energy, neighboring nodes, and distance to the sink. The proposed method attains the clustering quality accuracy of 97% and drastically decreases the run time with respect to the Ant-Based Clustering algorithm.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Smart Electric Meters in Morocco: A Perception Study
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving digital landscape, artificial intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming the global energy sector. Since 2016, Morocco's National Electricity and Drinking Water Office (ONEE) has been piloting the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) project, deploying AI-based smart meters to modernize the national electrical grid.
