The following work summarizes some recent and concrete contributions.

articleTitle: Impact of thermal-oxidative ageing on high-density polyethylene pipes: Analysis and prediction of service life
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: High-density polyethylene (HDPE) is increasingly used in the manufacture of culverts and drainage pipes because of its many advantages. The question of the longevity of HDPE pipes made from recycled resins compared with those made from virgin resins has aroused growing interest in the scientific community. Several recent studies have confirmed the high durability of HDPE, estimating its lifespan at over 100 years. However, external factors, such as environmental conditions and operating constraints, can influence this longevity. However, its oxidative thermal ageing is crucial to its durability. This study investigates the effects of thermo-oxidative ageing on the mechanical and physico- chemical properties of PE, highlighting the degradation mechanisms induced by prolonged exposure to high temperatures and oxygen. A method combining experimental tests and predictive modelling was developed to assess the lifetime of the materials. The Arrhenius model was used to estimate degradation kinetics and predict PE lifetime as a function of ageing conditions.

articleTitle: Revolutioning E Commerce : How Live Shopping Shapes Consumer Impulse Buying in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study explores the determinants of impulse buying within Live Stream Shopping applications, examining the impact of Physical Characteristic Similarity, Value Similarity, Product Attributes, Parasocial Relationships, Product Fit, Trust, and Perceived Product Quality. This research adopts a quantitative approach with primary data sources. Data collection was conducted using a questionnaire. The sample consists of 421 consumers who have experienced live streaming shopping. Purposive sampling was employed to select the participants. Data analysis was performed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with the assistance of Smart PLS statistical software. The results reveal that Physical Characteristic Similarity, Value Similarity, Product Attributes, Parasocial Relationships, and Trust significantly enhance Product Fit and Perceived Product Quality, which in turn drive Impulse Buying. This research underscores the importance of optimizing live stream shopping experiences to improve consumer satisfaction and highlights the growing role of live stream shopping in Indonesia's vibrant e-commerce landscape.

articleTitle: Information Success Model for FinTech Moderated by Trust
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The fast paced development of Financial Technology (FinTech), has revolutionized customers to use financial services. However, the ability of FinTech platforms to succeed is heavily influenced by factors like user satisfaction and trust. This study aims to evaluate the success of FinTech platforms, using the DeLone and McLean Information Systems (IS) Success Model, with trust as a moderating variable. We employ a quantitative approach and primary data gathered through surveys. The respondents of our study are users of FinTech, with usage of at least a year. Structural Equation Modelling is used to analyze the relationships between variables. The analysis conducted in this research indicates that User Satisfaction is significantly influenced by System Quality, Service Quality, and Service Quality moderated by Trust while User Satisfaction is not significantly influenced by Information Quality, System Quality moderated by Trust, and Information Quality moderated by Trust.

articleTitle: Energy-saving in steam systems: Case studies from the Moroccan industry - comparison and learned lessons
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The industrial sector accounts for a significant share of global energy consumption and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, with steam systems playing a critical role in process heating and power generation. This paper presents a comparative analysis of three case studies conducted in Morocco's pulp and paper, agri-food, and plastic industries, all of which are considered energy-intensive sectors. The objective is to assess the performance of these industries' steam systems using the Steam System Scoping Tool (SSST) and evaluate their system efficiencies. The study highlights energy-saving actions implemented in each case and demonstrates how simple maintenance measures, such as repairing steam leaks, controlling excess air, and improving insulation, can significantly enhance energy efficiency and reduce costs. By adopting a systems approach to steam optimization, the study proves that cost-effective actions with short payback periods can lead to substantial energy savings without requiring major capital investments. The annual cumulative financial savings across the three case studies amounted to $608,547, with energy savings of 40,987.65 GJ and an emissions reduction of 2,809.65 tons of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Despite focusing on different industries, the findings are applicable to a broad range of sectors, as the core components of steam systems are widely shared. Additionally, this work supports the African Union's Agenda 2063 and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by providing practical insights and recommendations for improving industrial energy efficiency and reducing environmental impact.

articleTitle: Micro- and Macro-Mechanical Behavior of Inter- and Intra-Laminar Hybrid Composite Laminates with Natural and Synthetic Fibers: RVE Modeling and Classical Laminate Theory
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study investigates the micromechanical and macromechanical behavior of hybrid composite laminates composed of flax and E-glass fibers in an epoxy matrix. At the microscale, effective mechanical properties are determined using Representative Volume Element (RVE) modeling with Periodic Boundary Conditions (PBC), validated against analytical models such as the Modified Halpin-Tsai and the rule of mixtures. At the macroscale, the laminate stiffness is evaluated using Classical Laminate Theory (CLT). Two hybridization configurations with symmetrical ply stacking sequences are analyzed: inter-laminar, where flax and E-glass fibers are distributed in separate plies, and intra-laminar, where both fiber types are combined within each ply. Both configurations maintain a total fiber volume fraction (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">f</inf>) of 0.5. Results show that the intra-laminar hybrid provides more balanced stiffness, whereas the inter-laminar configuration increases longitudinal stiffness but reduces transverse stiffness while enhancing shear properties. These findings provide insights into the influence of hybridization configurations on composite laminate performance.

articleTitle: The Convergence of AI and Blockchain Technologies: A Review on Enhancing IoT Security
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The fast expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT), especially in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), has brought significant security challenges, as interconnected devices have become key attacks for cyber threats. Traditional security techniques generally struggle to provide scalable, sufficient preservation. Therefore, this investigation examines the combination of blockchain and artificial intelligence (AI) as a possible solution to boost IoT security. Blockchain, a decentralized ledger technology, provides data integrity, transparency, immutable user authentication, and secure logging of transactions across several systems. Meanwhile, AI facilitates anomaly detection and predictive threat analysis by recognizing unexpected behaviors in network traffic. By utilizing past data, AI can anticipate possible cyberattacks, allowing industries to take preventive security measures. To resolve existing challenges, this investigation proposes the Artificial Intelligence Lightweight Blockchain Security Model (AILBSM), which combines trust management, blockchain-based privacy protection, and AI-driven attack detection throughout a designed three-level security layout. Initially, AILBSM assesses device authenticity to provide the reliability of IIoT sensors. Next, a lightweight blockchain algorithm is used for data authentication and attack prevention. Eventually, an AI-driven mechanism labels cyber threats, leveraging real-time security observation. AILBSM advances current solutions by minimizing processing load with a lightweight blockchain framework and strengthening protection through automated irregularity identification. Unlike standard models, which are power-consuming, AILBSM improves performance without compromising data integrity. This model empowers businesses to enhance security, optimize operations, make better decisions, and handle IoT issues while securing flexible digital safety.

articleTitle: Sentiment-Annotated Hibapress: A Moroccan News Arabic Dataset (SAHMNAD) predicted using Fine-Tuned Arabic Language Models and Zero-Shot LLMs
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study presents the Sentiment-Annotated Hibapress, a Moroccan News Arabic Dataset (SAHMNAD), a Moroccan news headlines dataset for sentiment analysis, sourced from a national digital news website, Hibapress, with user engagement metrics such as likes and dislikes as sentiment indicators. Unlike prior research focused on social media, this news headline data enables structured sentiment classification in mainly Modern Standard Arabic, addressing linguistic challenges unique to Moroccan digital news.We fine-tune Arabic-specific pretrained language models, including Asafaya-BERT and DarijaBERT, for sentiment classification and compare them with multilingual and general-purpose models. Asafaya-BERT achieves the highest accuracy of 90.74% with an F1 score of 90.58%, significantly outperforming zero-shot large language models such as BLOOM-560m with 78.76% and XLM-R with 66.04%, as well as multilingual models like DistilBERT with 88.65%. The results highlight the effectiveness of fine-tuned models for Moroccan Arabic sentiment classification.This research underscores the necessity of localized Arabic Natural Language Processing (NLP) models and explores large language models for zero-shot sentiment classification. Future directions include integrating reader comments, multimodal sentiment analysis, and cross-lingual approaches to further enhance sentiment classification in Moroccan digital media.

articleTitle: OneM2M-BasedAdaptive Loss Recovery mechanisms for enhancing Scalability and Quality of Service in IoT networks
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The technological world has known major advancements, leading to the creation of new paradigms like the Internet of Things (IoT). IoT is a combination between two concepts , the "Internet" and "Things" .This innovative notion connects billions of devices, enabling automation and smarter systems across industries like healthcare, smart cities, and manufacturing. By integrating concepts such as M2M, Big Data, and AI, IoT has transformed communication and innovation. However, as IoT networks expand, they face challenges like scalability, increased latency, limited bandwidth, and higher error rates, which impact Quality of Service (QoS).This paper proposes implementing Simple Automatic Repeat reQuest loss recovery mechanisms within IoT architecture to enhance QoS and address scalability challenges, ensuring reliable performance even as the network grows.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Storage Optimization in Stand-Alone PV-Fuel Cell DC Microgrid with Li-ion and Lead-Acid Batteries Storage
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The present paper deals with the implementation of Model Predictive Control for optimization of energy storage in the case of a stand-alone photovoltaic-fuel cell DC microgrid equipped with Li-ion and lead-acid batteries. This work begins by broadly introducing the general concept of MPC and its relation to microgrid energy management. Detailed explanations have been provided for problem formulation including the mathematical modeling of system dynamics, operational constraints, and optimization objectives. The proposed MPC framework is validated using two scenarios of simulation: one for a sunny day and the other for a cloudy day. The simulation results show the potential of MPC to handle the change in environmental conditions while maintaining operational constraints, efficient energy storage management, and increasing the overall performance of the microgrid. This work shows the potential of MPC for energy optimization and resilience in renewable energy-based microgrids.

articleTitle: Wearable Assistive Technologies for Blind People
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Wearable assistive technologies enhance autonomy and quality of life for blind individuals. This paper reviews the current state-of-the-art, considering advantages, limitations, and the growing impact of AI. It explores how machine learning and multimodal interfaces personalize and improve device efficiency, enabling more intuitive navigation, object recognition, and communication. The paper provides a concise overview and showcases representative works, highlighting both benefits like improved mobility and usability limitations.

articleTitle: Securing IoT Networks with Adversarial Learning: A Defense Framework Against Cyber Threats
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper responds to this increasing issue in the IoT domain by utilizing adversarial training methods to develop strong security solutions. Thus, to defend against the defense, we propose a defense framework that carry out Adversarial Training and Feature Squeeze to counteract adversarial attacks, FGSM, PGD. We validate the performances of these countermeasures for machine learning models (Decision Trees, SVM) and for a Deep Learning model (CNN) with a popular IoT-23 dataset. Results show that Adversarial training improves model robustness considerably when models are complex like CNN and SVM and they are brittle to these attacks. Such a dual-defensive model reduces risk and showcases pliability in handling a range of IoT provisioning environments. Our work highlights the opportunity for augmenting such defenses in practical IoT environments to improve resilience and security to dynamic and advanced cyber threats.

articleTitle: G-Net: A Novel Intrusion Detection Model for VANETs Based on Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) play a critical role in intelligent transportation systems by enabling seamless communication between vehicles and infrastructure. These networks optimize traffic management, enhance road safety, and support the development of autonomous driving technologies. However, their reliance on wireless communication makes them vulnerable to various security threats, necessitating robust intrusion detection systems (IDS). A network intrusion detection model based on deep learning has become a significant area of research to the growth of cyber threats and the limitations of traditional detection methods. Deep learning techniques, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), offer advanced capabilities for feature extraction, enabling more accurate detection of anomalies and malicious activities within network traffic. In this paper, we propose G-Net, a novel network intrusion detection model using convolutional neural networks CNNs for multi-class classification. This model is inspired by the gates mechanisms used in recurrent neural networks (RNNs) such as Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) and Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) networks. The proposed G-Net model allows to selectively focus on significant features in network traffic data while filtering out irrelevant information. The performance of the proposed intrusion detection model is evaluated on KDD-NSL dataset and compared with other existing works. Empirical results show that the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 98,57%, precision of 98,64%, recall of 98,57% and an F1-score of 98,58%, for 5-class classification using NSLKDD dataset. This model is able to automatically identify and classify several types of intrusions, including DoS, probe, R2L and U2R attacks. Therefore, it can be an effective and reliable solution for the intrusion detection.

articleTitle: From Emotion to Action: The Impact of Digital Emotional Intelligence and Digital Communication on Digital Teamwork among Indonesian Employees
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study examines how Digital Emotional Intelligence (DEI) and Digital Communication (DC) affect Digital Teamwork (DTW) in modern companies. Knowing digital teamwork principles is crucial as companies increasingly use virtual collaboration. Using a cross-sectional survey of Greater Jakarta employees, the study examined DEI's direct impact on DTW and DC's mediating role. Structural equation modelling (SEM) results show that directly and indirectly, DEI affects DTW by improving communication, emphasizing DEI as a key skill for digital cooperation. The findings show that emotional intelligence in digital environments improves communication, creating a harmonious and productive workplace. This study adapts emotional intelligence and communication theories to digital working environments to emphasize DEI and DC in virtual teamwork models. Practical implications suggest companies should support DEI and digital communication training to improve teamwork. Cross-sectional design and regional focus limit insights into digital teamwork in many environments. Future studies could use longitudinal and cross-cultural approaches.

articleTitle: Optimized Deep Learning Model for Early Parkinson’s Disease Detection Using Speech Spectrograms
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder, and early detection is crucial for timely intervention and management. This study proposes an innovative approach for non-invasive PD detection using deep learning techniques applied to speech analysis. Speech recordings of Parkinson’s patients and healthy individuals were converted into spectrograms using the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), which were then processed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction. We employed several convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, including CNN, MobileNet, ResNet50, and Inception, to classify the data. A 5-fold cross-validation was applied. Among the models, CNN demonstrated superior performance, achieving 99.19% accuracy, 100% precision, and 99.21% F1 score without cross-validation, which improved to perfect scores across all metrics when cross-validation was applied. The results indicate that deep learning, coupled with speech signal processing and cross-validation, provides a powerful tool for the early, non-invasive detection of Parkinson’s disease. This approach holds significant potential for improving diagnosis accuracy and enabling timely medical intervention.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Approach to Predict Remaining Useful Life of Rolling Bearings: OCP as case study
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Predictive maintenance is essential for minimizing downtime and optimizing the performance of critical industrial systems. In this study, we propose a machine learning-based approach to predict the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of rolling bearings, a critical component in phosphate grinding mills. Unlike traditional methods that rely on vibration data, our approach leverages operational data, including shift of work, phosphate layer, phosphate quality, working time, tonnage of rock and cumulative metrics. Two predictive models were developed: Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). Experimental results demonstrate the potential of ANN-based model to enable precise RUL predictions, facilitating proactive maintenance scheduling and reducing unplanned downtime. The proposed approach is cost-effective, utilizes existing historical data, and can be extended to other industrial equipment and defect types.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effects of Dimensionality Reduction Techniques on Topic Classification of an Arabic News Article Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: this study examines the difficulties of classifying text in Arabic using advanced machine learning (ML) algorithms with dimension reduction methods like Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP). Keeping in view the unique complexities of text in news articles written in Arabic, we employed diverse ML algorithms like Support Vector Machines (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Multinomial Naïve Bayes (MNB), and Random Forest. In comparative research, we examine the effect of PCA and UMAP on model performance with regard to accuracy and processing time. The findings indicate that PCA increases accuracy in all models with a maximum accuracy of 87.23% using SVM with PCA. Along with this, PCA reduces processing time significantly compared to processing raw text and is thus a good candidate to consider in text classification in large datasets. This research not only emphasizes the importance of dimension reduction in text classification in Arabic but also offers insights to enhance ML workflows in other languages with complex structures.

articleTitle: A Malware Detection Approach For Internet of Medical Things Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) revolutionizes healthcare by improving patient engagement, real-time monitoring, and data analysis through connected medical devices. However, the open and resource-constrained nature of IoMT networks introduces significant vulnerabilities, particularly to malware attacks that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of sensitive data and systems. These vulnerabilities pose serious risks to human life and the integrity of healthcare systems, making robust malware detection systems critical. Detecting unknown malware in IoMT environments remains a significant challenge for researchers and practitioners. Machine learning (ML) approaches have emerged as key tools for advancing intrusion detection, providing solutions to secure IoMT systems against evolving threats. This study proposes a low-cost, high-accuracy ML-based malware detection method for Windows PE files on medical devices and servers. Using the "Portable Executable (PE) malware" dataset, six ML algorithms were evaluated. Random Forest (RF) achieved the best results, with 99.28% accuracy and a processing time of 272 ms.

articleTitle: Library Search Engine Using Text Indexing from Scanned Thesis and Capstone Manuscripts
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Library Search Engine Using Text Indexing from Scanned Thesis and Capstone Manuscripts is implemented to address the challenges regarding the absence of a repository platform for the College of Computing Studies (CCS). Physical manuscripts limit accessibility for academic research, and without digital copies will only provide short-term preservation. The general objective is to develop a library search engine incorporating Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for scanned manuscripts into searchable text. Upon uploading the manuscript, the system automatically extracts metadata such as title, abstract, authors, and publication year. Methodologically, the Agile software model guides the development approach and descriptive statistics were used to visualize the collected data. Scanned manuscripts may be partially uploaded due to system limitations, but users can resume and complete the upload process seamlessly. Additionally, tracking the number of views for each manuscript helps showcase its popularity, providing valuable insights into user engagement and research interest. A satisfaction survey was conducted, yielding an average rating of 4.4. The findings confirm that advanced text indexing and OCR integration effectively preserve digital archives, minimize redundancy, and enhance research efficiency. The significance of a library search engine is to effectively manage academic manuscripts and enhance accessibility to relevant research and project development. It also showcases the achievement of students and the college, while CCS reputation will also be acknowledged as a hub for excellence. In conclusion, the integration of OCR in the system has proven effective in scanning manuscript recognition and text indexing to convert the scanned manuscript into searchable text.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fatigue Monitoring in Aircraft Wing Structures using Smart Sensor Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper proposes a smart fatigue monitoring system for aircraft wing structures, utilizing piezoelectric sensors, to detect stress, and actuators to mitigate risks in real-time. The integration of advanced machine learning algorithms, enables the analysis of sensor data against established thresholds, facilitating accurate predictions of potential fatigue conditions. A SolidWorks simulation focusing on a NACA 4412 airfoil wing is conducted to evaluate the system’s effectiveness under gravity, lift, and drag loads. Additionally, the paper discusses essential design considerations and provides a preliminary cost analysis. A Python-Based simulation is considered to further assess the system’s performance, achieving an accuracy of 97 % for the predictions models, with precision and recall metrics indicating robust classification capabilities. Hence, the suggested scheme promises high potential to enhance the monitoring and management of structural fatigue in aviation, ultimately leading to improved safety, reduced maintenance costs, and extended asset lifespan.

articleTitle: Sentiment analysis with XAI algorithm for movies recommendation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Movie streaming platforms rely on recommendation systems to suggest films, but users often don’t understand how these recommendations are made. This study combines Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) and sentiment analysis to create a recommendation system that not only suggests movies but also explains why they are recommended. By analyzing user moods and matching them with movie features, the system uses content-based filtering to provide personalized suggestions. XAI techniques make these suggestions clear and easy to understand, building trust and improving the user experience. This work shows how explainable systems can make movie recommendations smarter and more user-friendly.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Heat Sink Material on Processor Thermal Management
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: A heat sink functions as a passive cooling system, extracting heat from an electronic or mechanical device and transferring it to a fluid medium like air or liquid coolant. This process enables the regulation of the device's temperature to prevent overheating. The paper provides an overview of the current state of research on heat sink designs for processor cooling in laptops. The review discusses various materials for heat sink designs and their effectiveness in dissipating heat from electronic devices. There is a comparison between various materials other than aluminum and copper. Through that comparison, the paper determines the best alternative materials for aluminum and copper in a heat sink.

articleTitle: Discrete velocity method for rarefied gas flow within a microchannel
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study focuses on a classic fluid dynamics problem of gas Couette flow between two parallel plates in relative motion. The main objective of this research is to analyze the rarefaction degree impact on the transport characteristics of a rarefied gas flow, both in planar and oscillatory configurations, using the Discrete Velocity Method (DVM). Depending on its rarefaction, the flow can belong to different regimes: continuum, slip, transition, and free molecular. The study highlights the challenges of solving the Boltzmann equation, particularly in the transition regime. The DVM is used to solve the Boltzmann equation in the rarefaction regime, determining the velocity and shear stress profiles for the planar Couette flow and the amplitudes and phases in the oscillatory Couette flow. The obtained results are validated with other numerical methods, such as Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) and the linearized Boltzmann equation solution (BE). The results show a significant sensitivity of flow characteristics with the rarefaction intensity given by the Knudsen number (Kn). This shows the DVM’s accuracy as an effective and accurate alternative, particularly in slip and transition regimes. The study also extends to the analysis of oscillatory Couette flow, where the plates oscillate at a given frequency. This flow is analyzed using complex variables to capture the amplitudes and phases of the movement. This study demonstrates the applicability of DVM in practical situations, particularly in microfluidic and vacuum devices, where the understanding of flow characteristics is crucial.

articleTitle: From Queries to Understanding: Designing the Next-Generation Search Engine
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Imagine typing a question into a search engine and getting not just a list of blue links, but a thoughtful, accurate answer that understands exactly what you need. From queries to understanding, the way we access and interpret information has been transformed. This paper explores the evolution of intelligent information retrieval systems (IRS), particularly in the context of large language models (LLMs) and their implications for future IR research and applications. We aim to address critical questions regarding the strengths and weaknesses of LLMs in enhancing IR systems. We discuss traditional IR methods, their limitations, and the rise of LLMs, emphasizing the need for a balanced approach that combines retrieval and generation techniques to improve user experience and satisfaction. The paper proposes a framework for future research that leverages LLMs to create intelligent, transparent, and responsible information retrieval system (IRS).

articleTitle: How Relationship Management Moderates Burnout and Health Harm in the Indonesian Workplace: Emotional Intelligence View
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study examines the relationship between burnout and health harm in the workplace, with a focus on the moderating role of relationship management within emotional intelligence. A survey of 740 employees in Greater Jakarta, Indonesia, was conducted, using structural equation modeling (SEM) and partial least square (PLS) methodology to analyze the data. The results show a strong positive relationship between burnout and health harm but no significant moderating effect of relationship management. This suggests that while emotional intelligence may enhance interpersonal dynamics, it is not sufficient to mitigate the health risks associated with burnout. The study contributes to the limited literature on burnout and emotional intelligence in Indonesia, highlighting the need for direct interventions, such as workload adjustments and employee support programs. Future research could examine other factors that might moderate this relationship.

articleTitle: Nonfragile H∞ observer design for a class of One-Sided Lipschitz uncertain systems with quantization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper addresses the design of nonfragile observers for a class of one-sided Lipschitz nonlinear systems with quantization. The measured output signals undergo quantization through a static quantizer before transmission. To achieve this, the one-sided Lipschitz condition and the quadratic inner-bounded condition are used to derive less conservative criteria for observer design. By applying a decoupling technique, sufficient conditions are expressed in the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) to guarantee the robustness of the closed-loop system with quantization. Additionally, the observer gain is calculated. The proposed approach is validated using a practical example involving a mechanical rotating system.

articleTitle: Adaptive HEVC Transmission Using AI-Powered Predictive Bandwidth Management for Enhanced QoS
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: With the growing demand for high-quality video streaming, the necessity of efficient methods to balance video quality and bandwidth consumption has become increasingly critical to ensure seamless user experiences and optimize network resources. Traditional adaptive streaming techniques often respond to network fluctuations, leading to delays and quality degradation. In this paper, we introduce a new AI-powered approach for adaptive HEVC transmission that is trained to predict bandwidth variations and adjust the encoding parameters to ensure optimal Quality of Service. The proposed approach uses models trained on historical and real-time network data to guarantee seamless transitions and reduce buffering to ensure a better user experience overall. The results of this work demonstrate that our proposed system outperforms traditional techniques in terms of video quality and stability during network fluctuations.

articleTitle: Balancing AI Engagement: How AI Experience and Satisfaction Reduce Technostress among Indonesian Employees
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study explores the impact of AI experience, AI-based work engagement, and AI-based satisfaction on technostress among employees in Indonesia. It addresses the issue of how AI adoption affects workplace stress and employee satisfaction, offering insights into mitigating technostress through AI integration. The study uses a quantitative, cross-sectional design and multiple regression analysis to test hypotheses. Data was collected from employees across Indonesia via an online survey distributed through Google Forms. The findings show that AI experience has the strongest negative effect on technostress, meaning greater familiarity with AI tools reduces stress. In contrast, AI-based work engagement is positively linked to technostress, suggesting that higher engagement may increase stress. AI-based satisfaction is also negatively related to technostress, highlighting the importance of user-friendly systems. The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which restricts conclusions about long-term effects, and the convenience sampling method, which may not fully capture the diversity of organizational contexts. To reduce technostress, organizations should focus on enhancing AI experience through training, managing engagement to prevent burnout, and ensuring AI systems are user-friendly. This study contributes to the under-explored area of AI’s role in technostress, specifically in Indonesia, providing unique insights into AI’s influence on workplace dynamics.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent System for Semantic Extraction and Management of University Activities
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This work is part of a novel agent-based framework designed to analyze and process semi-structured information from web pages in order to generate semantic annotations. The primary objective is to develop a design approach that enables the automated generation of RDF annotations by extracting semi-structured data from web content.The study focuses on a real-world use case: a web platform dedicated to the management, capitalization of academic activities, and traceability of students and staff at the Faculty of Legal, Economic and Social Sciences of Ain Sebaâ (FSJES), Hassan II University of Casablanca (UH2C). The proposed solution leverages XML, XHTML, XSLT, and RDF technologies, and is guided by an ontology formalized in RDFS within the framework of the European CoMMA project (Corporate Memory Management through Agents). The extraction process is driven by a society of cooperating agents as the core methodological approach.The experimental results were encouraging and aligned well with the research goals. Specifically, the extractors successfully annotated the target web platform using a template derived from a representative page. Furthermore, the integration of learning techniques enhanced the generation and updating of extraction templates. Notably, the adoption of relative XPath expressions for locating data elements contributed to improved robustness and adaptability of the extraction process.

articleTitle: Determination of the Equivalence of Magnetic and Electric Mode Radiation Efficiencies in Advanced Metamaterial Antennas Through Characteristic Modes Theory
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach based on Characteristic Mode Theory (CMT) to improve radiation performance and compactness in metamaterial antennas by determining the equivalence between magnetic and electric modes for advanced applications. First, a comprehensive analytical study without excitation is conducted to evaluate the performance characteristics of Complementary Split Ring Resonator (CSRR) in terms of resonant frequencies and the radiation characteristics of electric resonant modes. Utilizing Coupled Mode Theory, we first identify the resonant modes that establish the equivalence between CSRR and Split Ring Resonator (SRR) structures. This approach simplifies the analysis by avoiding the complex task of directly determining the excitation modes of CSRR structures, which in turn significantly reduces the overall complexity. In fact, the equivalent SRR antenna, rather than its complementary counterpart, is excited with a coaxial probe feed in the dominant directional electric resonant mode to achieve exceptional radiation efficiency. The results demonstrate a strong correlation between the predictions derived from CMT and the S-parameter performance. Additionally, the proposed approach achieves a substantial 30% size reduction and improved radiation efficiency for the SRR antenna compared to conventional CSRR designs. The techniques outlined in this paper offer further potential for both size reduction and enhanced radiation performance in metamaterial-based antennas, setting the stage for more efficient and compact designs in future applications.

articleTitle: The Role of AI Experience and Satisfaction in Reducing Technostress in the Workplace: Managing the Digital Dilemma among Indonesian Employees
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study examines how AI-based satisfaction mediates the relationship between AI experience, technostress in the workplace, and AI satisfaction. The study explores how AI integration affects employee well-being and stress in Greater Jakarta workplaces. A quantitative research design used cross-sectional data from Greater Jakarta employees from various sectors. Analysis and hypothesis testing were done using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). AI experience positively affects AI-based satisfaction and negatively affects technostress, with AI-based satisfaction as a significant mediator. The findings emphasize the importance of AI experience and satisfaction in reducing technostress and improving employee well-being. Cross-sectional studies limit causal inferences, and data from one location may limit generalizability. Future studies should use longitudinal designs, examine other technostress factors, and include diverse cultural and organizational contexts. Organisations should improve AI user experience and satisfaction by providing user-friendly interfaces, training, and support. Technostress can be reduced, and employee engagement can be increased with this approach. There is limited research on the mediating role of AI-based satisfaction in the relationship between AI experience and technostress. This study provides new insights. Organisations can improve AI integration strategies with its thorough approach framework.

articleTitle: MEDCHAIN-SENEGAL: A Blockchain Solution for Medical Emergency Management
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study proposes an innovative private blockchain-based solution to improve medical emergency management in Senegal, especially in the context of road accidents that cause around 700 deaths per year. Faced with the major challenges of the Senegalese healthcare system—namely the lack of fast access to critical medical information for victims and the non-compliance with standards by 94% of Emergency Reception Services—our approach implements a technical architecture adapted to local constraints. The developed system integrates a three-level hierarchical access control, enabling secure and efficient management of emergency medical data while ensuring confidentiality. Based on Ganache and Web3.js technologies, our solution facilitates instant access to essential information such as blood type, allergies, and ongoing treatments, while guaranteeing complete traceability of access through the blockchain. The results show a significant improvement in emergency response time and better coordination among the different players in the rescue chain. This approach is part of the Ministry of Health’s 2022-2026 national strategic plan and offers a concrete solution to modernize Senegal’s healthcare system, paving the way for similar applications in other African countries facing comparable challenges.

articleTitle: Optimizing Training Hyperparameters for Multilayer Perceptrons in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Deep neural networks require an appropriate selection of hyperparameters for their operation. Among these, training hyperparameters, such as the learning rate, batch size, or the parameters of optimization algorithms, play an important role in the models’ convergence, accuracy, and generalization ability. This paper reviews the most influential training hyperparameters in the context of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). An analysis of recent studies highlights the approaches used to optimize these hyperparameters and their impacts on model performance. Finally, this paper explores current challenges related to the optimization of training hyperparameters and suggests future research directions.

articleTitle: Exploring Techniques and Countermeasures Against Browser Tracking: A Comprehensive Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Considering the scale of online privacy threats, it is crucial to investigate the effectiveness of current means of protecting users against these malicious methods. This paper examines recently developed techniques for preventing websites from tracking users' browsing habits without consent. We review tracking techniques based on client storage, such as cookies, including but not limited to supercookies and third-party cookies, in addition to HTML5 storage. We also present an advanced technique known as fingerprinting. The latter does not require storage on the device, like cookies, making it more difficult to bypass. Particular attention is given to behavioral tracking tools like mouse tracking. We talk about the legal rules and regulations that are currently in place. We also explain how it is possible to defend against them with the privacy protections of browsers (Firefox, Safari, and others.) and some extensions (uBlock Origin, AdBlock Plus, among others.) while examining the limits of these solutions.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Audit Quality in Non-Big Four Accounting Firm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Particularly in the context of Industry 4.0, artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing methods for solving problems and making decisions. AI is being used more and more in audits, which are crucial for guaranteeing the veracity and correctness of both financial and non-financial data, in order to increase productivity and effectiveness. Smaller accounting businesses are slower to implement AI than larger firms because of their conservative organizational cultures, lack of resources, and lack of experience. Using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), this study examines the factors influencing the adoption of AI by auditors in non-Big Four organizations and its effect on sustainable audit quality. The results show that performance and effort expectations are important factors in the adoption of AI, whereas social influence and favorable circumstances also play important but nuanced roles. The paper highlights implications for auditors and public accounting firms in improving audit quality and competitiveness, emphasizing the need for targeted training and organizational support to drive AI integration. To further understand and encourage the use of AI in auditing, future studies should include organizational and cultural aspects, longitudinal patterns, and qualitative insights.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Systematic Review of Deep Learning Techniques for Anomaly Detection in Urban Video Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The rapid evolution of urban surveillance systems has created an urgent need for advanced anomaly detection methods capable of interpreting complex public environments. This study employs the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology to evaluate deep learning's (DL) role in video-based anomaly detection. It contrasts conventional approaches with cutting-edge architectures like spatiotemporal convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), and transformer-based models. Our analysis demonstrates DL's superior performance over traditional methods across multiple benchmarks while revealing significant implementation challenges in real-world deployment, including computational complexity, cross-domain generalization, and ethical constraints. The study provides a comprehensive taxonomy of anomaly types, examines key evaluation metrics for operational systems, and identifies emerging solutions like edge-compatible lightweight models and privacy-preserving federated learning. By synthesizing a decade of research progress and practical limitations, this work offers actionable insights for developing robust, efficient, and socially responsible surveillance systems. The study proposes future directions focused on self-supervised learning, multimodal sensor fusion, and explainable AI frameworks to address critical gaps in urban security applications.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of stator unbalance in asynchronous machines using themography and statistics
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Innovation in maintenance practices and responsible resource management can play a key role in achieving global sustainable development goals. The integration of statistical analysis of thermographic data for fault diagnosis of three-phase induction motors (IMs) not only improves their performance, but also makes a significant contribution to the achievement of various Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Infrared thermography (IRT) is a non-contact, cost-effective and efficient method for real-time temperature monitoring and fault detection in electrical and mechanical machines. This paper examines the use of IRT for the diagnosis of stator unbalance (SU) in a IM. In this experimental work, thermal images were captured using a thermal imaging camera for a healthy-state IM, and the thermograms were then converted into usable data for in-depth statistical analysis. Measurements were carried out in three different conditions: healthy state, stator unbalance, and missing a phase. The results obtained were then compared using various statistical parameters, notably the skewness coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>), to evaluate the effectiveness of this thermographic and statistical method for diagnosing unbalance. The analyses show that the statistical description of the temperature distribution in the stator region of interest (ROI) is highly significant. Indeed, the values of the various parameters used clearly distinguish an unbalanced state from a healthy one. More specifically, an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> whose absolute value exceeds 2 is a reliable indicator of SU.

articleTitle: Advanced Thermal Energy Solutions: Phase Change Material Evaluation for Building
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research evaluates the effectiveness of two types of phase-change materials (PCMs): one paraffin-based (PCM1) and the other bio-based (PCM2), integrated within a multi-layer wall system. The thermal management and energy-saving capabilities of these MCPs were examined under diverse climatic conditions by numerical simulations performed with ANSYS 2021 R1. The results indicate that PCM1 is more efficient at storing latent heat, allowing it to maintain thermal conditions for extended durations, which makes it particularly suitable for regions experiencing constant temperature fluctuations. On the other hand, PCM2 reacts quickly to sudden temperature shifts because of its reduced melting point and enhanced thermal conductivity, optimizing performance across various environmental settings. Both PCMs markedly diminished indoor temperature fluctuations, achieving energy savings of roughly 18% for cooling requirements. Furthermore, PCM2's bio-based composition provides significant environmental benefits, consistent with sustainable construction methodologies. The results highlight the synergistic advantages of PCM1 and PCM2, stressing the necessity to customize PCM selection according to particular climatic and operational demands to improve building energy efficiency and thermal comfort. This research advocates for the incorporation of phase change materials into wall systems as an effective strategy for sustainable architectural solutions.

articleTitle: Alzheimer’s Detection via Cepstral Domain Feature Fusion and Mann-Whitney U-Test Statistical Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a robust approach for early detection of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) using advanced cepstral speech features, fused to capture diverse acoustic signatures. The Mann-Whitney U-test is employed to filter out non-informative features, improving real-world applicability and reducing overfitting. We systematically compare Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine classifiers, achieving an accuracy of 85.6% using only the most significant features, drawn from MFCCs, GTCCs, LPCCs, and others. The method addresses data sparsity challenges in clinical research by favoring domain-relevant indicators while maintaining computational feasibility. The results confirm that subtle vocal cues, captured using affordable devices, are promising biomarkers for AD screening, especially in resourcelimited or telehealth environments. By highlighting both practical implementation and scalability, our study contributes to the development of efficient, non-invasive diagnostic protocols. This, in turn, supports earlier intervention and improved patient outcomes. The framework thus paves the way for future multimodal expansions.

articleTitle: Refined Channel Estimation for Cell-Free Massive MIMO in Dense Urban Environments Using MMSE and Deep Feedforward Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper investigates a Cell-Free Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system for next-generation Fifth/ Sixth Generation (5G/6G) wireless networks, focusing on channel estimation under dense-urban conditions with numerous obstacles (e.g., buildings, trees). We first employ a linear Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) estimator to derive the channel state information (CSI) between user equipments (UEs) and access points (APs). While MMSE performs effectively in moderate-to-high signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), it shows limitations at low SNR or in harsh propagation scenarios where path loss and obstructions severely degrade the pilot signals. To overcome these shortcomings, we introduce a Deep Feedforward (DFF) neural network with multiple wide hidden layers (e.g., 3000, 2000, 1500 neurons) to predict the residual mismatch between the true channel and the MMSE estimate. By adding the learned correction to the initial MMSE estimate, our approach substantially reduces the bit error rate (BER) across all tested SNR levels, with pronounced improvements in challenging conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this refined estimator in a 1000m×1000m setting containing 200 UEs and 200 APs, highlighting its promise for high-density Cell-Free Massive MIMO deployments in future 5G/6G networks.

articleTitle: Internet of Energy in Microgrids and Smart Grids: State-of-the-Art
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Internet of Energy (IoE) represents a transformative paradigm that integrates internet technologies into energy systems, enabling enhanced monitoring, control, and optimization of energy resources. This paper provides a comprehensive state-of-the-art review of IoE applications in microgrids and smart grids. The review examines critical enabling technologies including advanced communication protocols, data analytics tools incorporating machine learning and big data approaches, and essential cybersecurity measures for energy infrastructure protection. In microgrids, IoE facilitates improved energy management, seamless integration of renewable energy sources, and enhanced resilience against disruptions. In smart grids, IoE enables grid automation, real-time demand response mechanisms, and consumer engagement through smart metering and dynamic pricing. The paper also addresses significant implementation challenges including interoperability issues, data privacy concerns, and the need for robust regulatory frameworks. By synthesizing current research and developments, this review highlights IoE’s potential to revolutionize energy systems while identifying critical areas requiring further investigation. The discussion demonstrates how IoE applications align with pressing energy concerns including security, sustainability, and scalability in the evolving global energy landscape.

articleTitle: Enhanced Deep Neural Network-Based Vehicle Detection System Using YOLOv11 for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study presents an advanced vehicle detection framework based on YOLOv11, the latest evolution of the YOLO family of object detectors. The model is tailored for real-time autonomous driving scenarios, addressing longstanding challenges such as false detections, missed targets, and diverse environmental conditions. Building on previous YOLO iterations, YOLOv11 introduces architectural innovations, including the C3k2 block, SPPF module, and C2PSA units, resulting in superior precision, recall, and inference speeds. A dataset of 30,000 images, spanning six vehicle categories E-Scooter, bicycle, bus, car, motorcycle, and truck was used for training, validation, and testing. Rigorous evaluations yielded a precision of 97.2%, recall of 93.4%, mAP@50 of 97.0%, and mAP@50-95 of 86.6%. These metrics underscore YOLOv11’s robustness and adaptability to complex environments, ensuring consistently high detection accuracy and minimal misclassification. Ultimately, YOLOv11’s enhanced performance and efficiency position it as a promising solution for intelligent transportation systems (ITS), adaptive traffic control, and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS).

articleTitle: Quantitative Reaction Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: We propose a new variant of reaction system that intends to take into account a few aspects of a biological reaction that have been considered at most partially in former works. These aspects are: (i) in the former variants, all the substances of the substrate completely vanish after identifying the set of reactants such that the result does not contain any former component of the substrate unless it is produced by the reaction, (ii) in any substrate, each element is either present in an arbitrary large number of copies, or it is not present at al, (iii) the effect of any inhibitor is the same but in biology the effect of inhibitors may be different due to their type. Our model considers multisets of reactants such that it is a more quantitative model than a qualitative one, inhibitors may be of different types such that their role may vary depending on the substrate, the substances that are not involved in the reaction remain in the substrate. We consider a parallel mode of enabling the reactions and prove that this mode may be simulated by sequential enabling. Later on, we define a computational model based on quantitative reaction systems and prove that their computation power equals that of multiset Turing machines.

articleTitle: Advancing Parkinson’s Disease Detection: A Review of AI and Deep Learning Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Neurodegenerative in nature, Parkinson's disease primarily impacts motor and non-motor processes with resultant significant detriments to the quality of life. In fact, for this reason, an early diagnosis becomes imperative—the appropriate application of intervention treatment often hampers an already conventional type of diagnosis. Thereby, clinical diagnosis remains mostly subjective. Advances in some state-of-the-art computational algorithms open new pathways offering noninvasive scalable solutions toward early detection. These approaches employ manifold modalities, ranging from voice analysis to wearable sensors, and hybrid machine learning frameworks, with diagnosis accuracy going as high as 97% in some cases. The major contributions are: Enhanced Smallest Normalized Difference Associative Memory, advanced nonlinear speech analysis techniques, telemonitoring systems that enable the remote monitoring of symptoms, and hybrid feature selection models such as HEFS-MLDR, which integrates dimensionality reduction with ensemble learning methodologies. While these are promising developments, a number of open challenges remain: dependence on high-quality data, generalizability across diverse populations is limited, and hybrid models are computationally intractable. Recent studies also highlighted that more work is needed to be done on developing better integration of multimodal data, more interpretable AI models, and clinical validation across diverse populations for broad generalizability. On the other hand, notwithstanding the mentioned difficulties, advances in computational methods have underlined the potential of these approaches for further improvement in diagnostic systems toward more accessible, more accurate, and efficient early diagnosis of Parkinson's disease.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Intelligent Transport Systems for Smart Cities: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The study provides a basic literature review of how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be used in developing smart transportation systems for cities. transport systems are evolving to prioritize sustainability by integrating advanced technologies and innovative approaches. Efforts to reduce CO₂ emissions include transitioning to electric transports, utilizing renewable energy sources, and adopting policies like urban densification and improved public transport networks. Technologies such as IoT, Big Data, and AI enhance real-time traffic management, predict mobility patterns, and optimize transport networks, while Intelligent Transport Systems reduce congestion, support autonomous vehicles, and facilitate multimodal transport. Mobility as a Service (MaaS) platforms, powered by AI, combine various transport modes into a single digital solution, offering personalized and sustainable mobility options while minimizing congestion and emissions. These innovations collectively transform urban mobility into more efficient, accessible, and environmentally friendly systems. This article also touches some of the limitations and challenges related to AI in transportation that previous researches has faced, such as the need for transparency, privacy concerns, and development cost.

articleTitle: Learning in Medical Image Segmentation: SAM Fine-Tuning vs. U-Net Training for Breast Ultrasound
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Breast cancer diagnosis and treatment planning rely on precise tumor segmentation in medical imaging. Deep learning models, particularly CNNs and Transformer-based architectures, have shown strong potential in automating this task. This study compares U-Net, a widely used CNN-based model, with the Segment Anything Model (SAM), a Vision Transformer pre-trained on natural images, for breast ultrasound tumor segmentation. While U-Net was trained from scratch on a breast ultrasound dataset, SAM was fine-tuned using prompt-based learning with bounding box annotations. The models were evaluated using IoU, Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), accuracy, precision, and recall. Experimental results show that fine-tuned SAM achieved an IoU of 0.9311, surpassing U-Net while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. Additionally, SAM’s ability to generalize across different breast tumor types highlights the potential of transformer-based architectures in medical imaging.This study provides insights into the trade-offs between CNN-based and transformer-based models for ultrasound tumor segmentation, emphasizing the impact of transfer learning and fine-tuning in adapting large-scale models to specialized medical applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Automotive Embedded Systems Security: Blockchain Solutions for Connected Vehicles and Supply Chain Management
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The security of automotive embedded systems and their associated supply chains is becoming increasingly critical due to the rise in cyber threats targeting these systems. As vehicles incorporate more advanced functionalities and are interconnected, they become more vulnerable to cyber-attacks. This article explores integrating blockchain technology to enhance the security and reliability of automotive embedded systems and supply chain management. The study discusses how blockchain can address various security challenges by providing secure communication protocols, enabling proactive maintenance, and ensuring compliance with industry standards. It highlights the potential of blockchain in autonomous vehicles, vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, and the broader automotive supply chain. By leveraging blockchain’s decentralized and cryptographic features, the research presents solutions to improve safety, reliability, and compliance in the automotive industry. The findings suggest that blockchain technology, combined with established standards and methodologies, can significantly mitigate security risks, and enhance the overall performance of automotive embedded systems.

articleTitle: Real estate market scoring
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Technological developments, especially in the areas of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Artificial Intelligence (AI), are causing a major shift in the real estate sector. From development to sales, these tools are improving different stages of the real estate industry. By putting forth a model for market scoring, we investigate in this article how GIS and machine learning can enhance property valuation. This model focuses on key features that affect property values, alongside the necessary AI algorithms and GIS analyses. Our research shows that important factors include proximity to amenities and infrastructure, which greatly influences property desirability. By using the XGBoost algorithm, we can evaluate different locations and assign appropriate scores based on these features. Analyzing data from 30 districts in Morocco, we emphasize the importance of proximity in valuation and present a scoring model that serves as a valuable resource for real estate stakeholders navigating today's market.

articleTitle: The Role of AI Influencers in Shaping Consumer Behavior: Analyzing Impulsive Buying through Perceived Value and Positive Emotional Appeal
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research aims to investigate the characteristics of AI Influencers, namely attractiveness, trustworthiness, and personalization of impulsive buying through perceived value and positive emotional appeal. To achieve this goal, the research approach used is a quantitative approach, with the data source being primary data. The data collection method uses a questionnaire distributed online. The number of samples in this research was 163, with the sampling technique being purposive sampling. The research results show that attractiveness has a significant effect on perceived value and positive emotional appeal, personalization influences perceived value and positive emotional appeal, perceived value influences impulsive buying, and positive emotional appeal has an effect on impulsive buying. Another result of this research is that trustworthiness has no effect on perceived value and positive emotional appeal.

articleTitle: Augmenting Moroccan Darija Text Data for Improved Classification: A Comparative Study of Augmentation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The performance of learning models mostly depends on the availability and quality of training data. To address the issue of dataset adequacy, researchers have widely investigated Data Augmentation (DA) as a promising solution. This paper examines the application of data augmentation techniques for the Moroccan Darija dialect, an under-resourced language with limited linguistic resources. We investigate using four Easy Data Augmentation (EDA) methods—Random Swap, Random Deletion, Random Insertion, and Synonym Replacement—to increase the diversity of training data, ultimately improving the performance of machine learning models. These techniques were applied to a corpus of Moroccan Darija sentences to improve text classification tasks for emotion detection (Fear, Anger, and Joy). The results demonstrate that these augmentation techniques can significantly enhance data variability, leading to more robust models for the Darija dialect. By creating synthetic examples, this approach tackles the issue of data scarcity in Moroccan Darija, ultimately improving performance in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks for low-resource languages.

articleTitle: Managing Access Control for AI APIs via Blockchain Smart Contracts
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: AI has already begun to lead transformation across industries, along with AI APIs such as predictive modeling and Natural Language Processing. Just like them, AI applications are on the rise as well. Unfortunately, those typically operate under the hackneyed idea of having a universal centralized access control entity, which are not only prone to security breaches, rather they lack efficiency and access transparency as well. Consequently, this hinders attempts made to secure sensitive data and enforce accountability in AI systems. This paper proposes a new system model based on blockchain technology and smart contracts and discusses how it manages access control to AI APIs. This solution tackles the limitations of conventional systems such as security, scalability, and transparency brought by decomposing access rights. There are different possibilities for monitoring and enforcing security policies, One of them, Dynamic access control prevents unauthorized users from gaining access to any resource. In addition, blockchain guarantees auditing by virtue of its decentralized nature, eliminating reliance on central entities. The proposed approach is substantiated through a combination of simulations alongside proof-of-concept implementations, demonstrating the ability to decrease access latency, enhance resistance to rogue access attempts and access management processes. This work increasingly enhances the decentralized security solutions available by providing an effective solution for access control in the context of centralized AI API’s for both enterprise and government use cases being scalable and robust as well as transparent.

articleTitle: AI and Supply Chain Resilience trends in the Automotive Industry: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This systematic literature review (SLR) explores the evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its impact on Supply Chain Management & Resilience, with a focus on the automotive industry. It examines how AI has transformed Supply Chain Management (SCM) from the early 2000s to the present, highlighting key advancements such as intelligent demand forecasting, and autonomous logistics. Although AI has been a subject of interest since the 1950s and has shown potential in improving decision-making and productivity, its integration into SCM is relatively recent.The review investigates both the challenges and opportunities associated with integrating AI into automotive supply chain. It outlines benefits such as enhanced efficiency, better decision-making, and increased resilience, while also addressing limitations including potential biases and the necessity for human oversight. By supporting a deeper understanding of AI’s role in enhancing supply chain management and resilience, the review provides insights into how AI can contribute to more intelligent and resilient supply chains. It also suggests areas for future research to advance the field further.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Performance of Hybrid Microgrids through Turbulent Flow-Based Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents the Enhanced Turbulent Flow of Water-Based Optimization (ETFWO), a novel algorithm designed to enhance energy management in hybrid microgrids. With the increasing global demand for energy and the pressing need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, hybrid microgrids that integrate renewable energy sources such as solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind power with conventional generators are becoming increasingly vital. The ETFWO algorithm utilizes the chaotic dynamics of turbulent flow to optimize real-time energy production, storage, and consumption, effectively addressing the challenges posed by the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources.

Author Keywords: Enhanced Turbulent Flow of Water-Based Optimization (ETFWO)

articleTitle: Optimization Of Accounting Recording Process Using RPA Technology in Multifinance Companies
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study investigates the optimisation process of accounting recording systems within financial institutions, focusing on the role of Robotic Process Automation in multi- finance firms. By employing a qualitative exploratory approach through a Systematic Literature Review, the research evaluates the extent to which existing studies have explored five key steps of process optimisation: Tasks and Process Identification, Workflow Redesign, Development and Testing, Implementation, and Performance Monitoring. The findings reveal that Tasks and Process Identification have received the most attention among these steps, while Development and Testing remain the least explored areas. The study highlights the transformative potential of Robotic Process Automation in enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and decision-making within financial operations. Furthermore, it provides insights into the challenges and opportunities for improving Robotic Process Automation implementation, suggesting a need for further research in less explored dimensions. This research contributes to understanding the current state of adoption and offers actionable insights for future advancements in the financial sector.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical evaluation of the performance of a photovoltaic panel in a semi-arid climate
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) solar energy is playing an increasingly important role in the global energy mix, thanks to its renewable potential and low environmental impact. However, the performance of PV systems varies considerably according to climatic and geographical conditions, making it essential to select the right technology for the region in question. In this study, the annual performance of a glass-tedlar PV panel was evaluated in a semi-arid climate. Experimental data were compared with the results of a numerical model developed in COMSOL Multiphysics. This model aims to predict the behavior of PV systems in specific environments, offering an economical alternative to the often-costly direct acquisition of technology. The results show that January is the best-performing month, with an average power of 153.4 W (around 61% of nominal power) and a maximum efficiency of 15.5%, in line with the low temperatures. On the other hand, August and October recorded the lowest output, with 132.1 W and 130 W respectively, and a minimum efficiency of 12.9% in August. The good agreement between simulated and experimental data confirms the model’s reliability, which can be adapted to other technologies and climates.

articleTitle: Examining the antecedents of food photo posting behavior on Instagram
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: "Foodstagramming" is a business phenomenon that has received attention from academics and practitioners. However, there are still limited studies on the driving factors of "foodstagramming." Therefore, this study aims to examine the factors that drive the behavior of posting food photos, including self-expression, online supportive interaction, and dine-in experience, identified as antecedent factors.
